Thick bile rose in her throat. At first it tasted like sadness, but now it left the bitter taste of rage in her mouth. A sound erupted from her body. It was a loud roar that echoed around the room as though it were coming straight at them. "Oh, my God," she whispered to herself through clenched teeth. "I'm dying." She breathed out slowly and carefully until she could catch her breath again. Her eyes grew wide when they reached the back door. The door had been chained shut behind her by someone who didn't know what he was doing or why he was putting up such a barrier. They'd done this before just for kicks, but not anymore since something called the Gate had opened between the two worlds where all the other barriers fell away, allowing this gate to be built. She knew there would come a day when she wouldn't even have to go outside because this barrier was going to stop her from ever leaving. For now, however, she couldn't stay here and wait for her time to escape. She had to get out. Her fingers twitched with hunger, and the more she tried to ignore it, the worse it got. She paced nervously on the top rail of the window seat, swaying back and forth just trying to keep her balance. Finally, she stopped moving and wrapped her legs tightly around the rails so that she could grip them tight enough to hold onto the railing without falling over. With every movement, she felt stronger and more determined than before. Finally, she arrived at the bottom of the stairs. She heard footsteps approaching in the darkness, then the sound of a mouse scurrying across the floorboards toward the stairs. She waited to see if he made his way down into the basement. When nothing happened, she assumed he hadn't gotten far enough yet. She watched him disappear around the corner at the end of the stairwell. The next few minutes passed with relative calm. She thought about calling 911, but decided against it instead. Instead, she climbed slowly up one flight of stairs after another until finally she reached a landing on the second level. There was a steel door leading off the landing and down into the tunnel beneath it. She pulled open the metal casing and pushed the heavy doors inward to reveal an endless hallway lined with cages filled with animals. As soon as the lights came on, she realized she was still alone. To her surprise, she saw three crates stacked neatly along each side of the corridor. Each crate held exactly ten cats and dogs. One dog lay curled up on its stomach, looking tired and sad. The others looked hungry, too, though, and she wondered how long they had been asleep. Then she noticed it - the cage behind the cat with the feline carrier. Caught in was a small, black kitten lying face-up on its belly in a tiny cage with just enough room for one arm. For a moment she stood frozen; then she remembered she had to carry the kitty before she could leave. She hurriedly turned around and held up both her arms, staring down at the tiny cat lying cradled inside. And then she cried. Annie picked up the little black kitty and put it gently into the cage. The poor thing barely moved beyond its mommy's touch, but Annie could tell it loved her very much. She set the kitty back into the cage and covered it loosely with some carpeting to make sure no one else touched it. Then she crawled down the last staircase and headed for the exit. At the doorway to the underground parking lot, she paused. Most people saw cars driving downtown during rush hour, but Annie knew better than most that they would never drive down to this part of town. The Harlem Renaissance was a cultural and intellectual movement that took place in the African-American community in the 1920s and 30s. It was a time of great change and growth for black Americans, marked by an explosion of artistic expression in fields such as music, literature, and visual arts. This period saw the emergence of many groundbreaking artists who challenged traditional norms and stereotypes, creating works that celebrated black culture and identity. In this essay, we will explore some of the key figures and themes of the Harlem Renaissance, and examine how their work continues to influence contemporary culture today.

At the heart of the Harlem Renaissance were its writers, poets, and intellectuals. One of the most famous authors of this era was Langston Hughes, whose poetry captured the soul of the black experience in America. His poem "The Negro Speaks of Rivers" speaks to the deep roots of black history and culture, from the Nile to the Mississippi. Another influential writer was Zora Neale Hurston, who penned novels such as "Jazz" and "Their Eyes Were Watching God," which explored the lives of black women in the rural South during the early 20th century. These works helped to give voice to the experiences of ordinary black people, often marginalized in mainstream American society.

In addition to its literary achievements, the Harlem Renaissance also had a profound impact on music. Jazz, blues, and gospel music all flourished during this period, with legendary performers such as Louis Armstrong and Duke Ellington leading the way. These musicians drew upon African rhythms and melodies, combined with European harmonies and instrumentation, to create a unique sound that spoke to both black and white audiences alike. Jazz became a symbol of freedom and liberation for many young black Americans, offering an alternative to the stifling racism and segregation they faced every day.

Visual arts also played a significant role in the Harlem Renaissance. Many black artists began creating works that depicted scenes of urban life, using vibrant colors and bold brushstrokes to capture the energy and vitality of the city streets. Aaron Douglas, one of the leading painters of the era, created powerful murals that showcased black heroes and mythology, such as his iconic image of the Madonna and Child set against a backdrop of African masks and textiles. Other notable artists included Jacob Lawrence, Romare Bearden, and Archibald Motley Jr., all of whom pushed the boundaries of what was considered acceptable in terms of subject matter and technique.

One of the defining characteristics of the Harlem Renaissance was its emphasis on black pride and self-determination. After centuries of oppression and dehumanization, many black Americans felt empowered to assert their own cultural identities and values. They sought to celebrate their heritage rather than trying to assimilate into dominant white culture. This spirit of self-affirmation is evident throughout the works of the Harlem Renaissance, whether in the lyrics of jazz songs or the imagery of paintings and sculptures. For example, James VanDerZee's photographs of African-American families and communities captured the beauty and dignity of black life at a time when these qualities were largely ignored or disparaged.

Despite its many accomplishments, however, the Harlem Renaissance was not without its challenges. Many of its leaders and supporters faced harassment and persecution from law enforcement, political opponents, and even members of their own communities. Some critics accused the movement of being too radical or militant, while others felt that it did not do enough to address issues of social justice and equality. Despite these criticisms, however, the legacy of the Harlem Renaissance has endured long after its heyday in the 1920s and 30s. Today, scholars continue to study its impact on everything from hip-hop and rap music to contemporary art installations and fashion trends. Its message of self-love and empowerment remains just as relevant today as it was nearly a century ago, inspiring new generations of artists and activists to carry forward its vision of racial justice and equity.

In conclusion, the Harlem Renaissance stands out as one of the most important periods in American cultural history due to its extraordinary array of talented individuals contributing to various forms of art; including music, literature, visual arts, and more. By examining their contributions and the context in which they worked, we gain insight into the struggles and triumphs experienced by Black Americans during this tumultuous period. Moreover, through studying their lasting legacies, we may better understand our shared human experience and appreciate the vast range of perspectives that make up our collective cultural identity. Ultimately, the Harlem Renaissance serves as a reminder of the power of art to transform societies, uplift marginalized voices, and bring us closer together across lines of race, ethnicity, gender, class, sexual orientation, ability, age, religion, national origin, immigration status, body size & shape - so let’s keep learning about this remarkable period!

Different Causes of Legal Action Report (Assessment)

Introduction

The case under analysis illustrates different causes of legal action, arising out of various situations. It is possible to single out several ones, for instance, trespassing, defamation, product negligence, violent assault, unpremeditated murder, and many others. Certainly, not all hypothetical lawsuits are likely to succeed because many of them may not be sufficiently grounded. Occasionally, the fact of misdemeanor is impossible to substantiate. The examples, which will be discussed in this paper, are entirely hypothetical yet, there are very widespread in modern practice. Moreover, they may be disputed for a very long period of time. This is why it is vital to overview probable solutions to these problems.

Main body

For instance, Labory hurts himself during one of his experiments with the toaster. In particular, he tried to cook a chicken on this device this lead to injury. In theory, Labory can sue the manufacturer (Great Toaster Inc) because the company did not warn the clients that this utensil was not intended for this purpose. Some of such lawsuits did yield results and the claimant was compensated. Yet, under these circumstances, Labory can hardly expect any indemnity for his misfortunes, because there is such concept as reasonable use of the product. In other words, a sensible person of his age is rather unlikely to cook a chicken in a toaster, and Great Toaster Inc cannot possibly presume that their toasters can be employed in such away. However, there is one limitation: provided that such incidents had occurred to a child, this enterprise might have been forced to pay money. The thing is that a child cannot be called a sensible person in every sense of this word. Therefore, the exact decision-making of the judge may vary.

Another interesting example is the relationship between trespassing and negligence of the premises. The students try to get into the house; they attempt to climb over a wooden, being unaware that the fence is on the verge of collapsing. The fence collapses and some of them fall on the broken glass. There is a great likelihood that they bring legal action against the owner of the house for alleged premises liability. We should bear in mind that the proprietor of the real estate has an obligation to notify his or her guests about dangerous conditions in the house or apartment especially if it may entail serious bodily injuries or death. But this rule does not include undiscovered trespassers. We need to take into consideration that these students were not invited to the party and had no right to intrude into the private territory. In the eyes of law, they are actually trespassers; this is why they are not eligible for any indemnity. Apart from that, the owner of the house might not even know about the damage. Finally, even a new fence can crash if it is being climbed over by many people at the same time and they might have possibly made a reasonable assumption of risks associated with their behavior. So this suit will be fruitless.

We may also need to discuss such causes of legal action as defamation when Cory claims that his friend Armorys sexual life is very promiscuous and adds Armory has all kinds of sexually transmitted diseases (STDs). This is one of those situations when a claimant (Armory) can file a lawsuit against Cory because the defendant deliberately tarnished his good name and reputation. The only defense under this scenario is the truth: Cory has to prove that his statement is grounded in any way. We need to take into account that Armory does not have any STDs. Cory may also argue that his intention was to protect the well-being of another person, Shelly. At first glance, this may seem to be a plausible explanation. However, defamation took place in the course of a quarrel and its primary cause was malice rather than good intention. Cory may as well tell that he was genuinely mistaken when he was insulting Armory. But even these defense tactics will be helpless because he could not receive this information from anyone. So Armory has every reason to believe that the compensation will be made.

This discussion should also include such cases as injury, inflicted in the course of outdoor games. Rory improperly tackles one of his friends Softy, his tackle results in broken ribs and hospitalization for three weeks. Rorys behavior can be interpreted as the cause for legal action, especially given the cost of medication for Softy. Yet, it is hardly probable that this lawsuit will succeed, because they were playing football, this sport is believed to be one of the most dangerous ones. Therefore, an individual who decides to play accepts hypothetical dangers. Nonetheless, there is an exception to this rule; namely if this harm was intentional and done out of malice. It is rather difficult for a judge to bring any verdict in such cases because the guilt of the defendant is almost impossible to prove.

Unpremeditated murder is by far the most crucial example, presented in this case. Shelly was running his car through the red light and collided with another vehicle. She tried to stop her car but it was too late and the other woman, an elderly lady did not survive the injuries. Naturally, Sheilas guilt is quite obvious.

From a legal perspective, she has committed an unintentional murder. Still, the court can justify her due to her emotional state. It should be mentioned that she was very upset by the quarrel in the house. Secondly, she did almost everything to avert the tragedy. These are extenuating circumstances, which may significantly affect the judgment of the court.

When speaking about Sheilas emotional distress we should discuss the accident that occurred in the house. As it has been pointed out earlier, Cory and Armory were quarreling with one another. Cory swung a bottle at Armory and barely hit Shelly. This may be interpreted as the infliction of emotional distress. Theoretically, this is grounds for a lawsuit because Corys behavior posed an immediate threat to Shellys health or even life. In case of trial, the claimant will be eligible for indemnity, especially if her claims are supported by witnesses testimony.

Conclusion

These scenarios illustrate the cases which have become quite common nowadays. They are very helpful to students, lawyers, judges, and average citizens, who should be familiarized with their rights and obligations. They are of great assistance to us because they illustrate the factors to which they need to pay attention, such as the presence or absence of the premeditation, motive, and awareness of committing the crime. Certainly, this discussion lacks specific details because in real-life situations the decision-making becomes much more complicated.

Animal experimentation has long been a controversial topic in the field of biomedical research. On one hand, it is argued that such experiments are essential for the advancement of medical knowledge and the development of new treatments. On the other hand, there are ethical considerations that raise concerns about the treatment of animals and the validity of using them as models for human diseases. In this essay, we will explore the ethical considerations of animal experimentation in biomedical research, weighing the benefits against the potential harm inflicted upon animals.

First and foremost, it is important to acknowledge the significant contributions that animal experimentation has made to medical science. Many of the medications and treatments we have today would not have been possible without the use of animals in research. Animals have been used to test the safety and efficacy of drugs, to study the progression of diseases, and to develop surgical techniques. Through these experiments, researchers have gained valuable insights into the functioning of the human body and have been able to develop life-saving treatments for various diseases.

However, despite these advancements, there are ethical concerns surrounding the use of animals in research. One of the main arguments against animal experimentation is the issue of animal welfare. Animals used in biomedical research are often subjected to painful procedures, confinement, and sometimes even euthanasia. It is argued that this is a violation of their rights and that it is morally wrong to cause harm to sentient beings for the benefit of humans. Animals are capable of feeling pain and suffering, just like humans, and therefore it is argued that their interests should be taken into consideration.

Furthermore, there is a growing concern about the validity and reliability of using animals as models for human diseases. While animals share many biological similarities with humans, there are also significant differences. These differences can result in misleading or inconclusive results when extrapolating findings from animal studies to humans. For example, many drugs that have shown promise in animal studies have ultimately failed in human clinical trials. This raises questions about the ethical justification for using animals when the results may not be applicable to humans.

In response to these ethical concerns, there has been a push to develop alternative methods to animal experimentation. Advances in technology have made it possible to use human cells, tissues, and computer models to simulate human physiological processes and study diseases. These methods, known as in vitro and in silico models, have the potential to replace or reduce the use of animals in research. By focusing on human-based models, researchers can minimize the ethical concerns associated with animal experimentation while still advancing medical knowledge.

However, it is important to note that there are limitations to these alternative methods. While they can provide valuable insights, they cannot fully replicate the complexity of the human body. Animal models still play a crucial role in understanding the fundamental mechanisms of diseases and testing the safety and efficacy of potential treatments. Without animal experimentation, it would be difficult to make significant progress in biomedical research and the development of new therapies.

In conclusion, the ethical considerations of animal experimentation in biomedical research are complex and multifaceted. While there are valid concerns about animal welfare and the validity of using animals as models for human diseases, it is also important to recognize the significant contributions that animal experimentation has made to medical science. As technology advances, there is a need to continue exploring alternative methods that minimize harm to animals while still advancing our understanding of human health. Ultimately, striking a balance between the pursuit of knowledge and the ethical treatment of animals is a challenge that requires ongoing dialogue and consideration.

In the grand tapestry of democratic societies, civic participation and voting are not merely threads but the very warp and weft that give the fabric its strength and color. The significance of these democratic processes lies in their ability to empower individuals, foster community engagement, and shape the trajectory of governance. The act of casting a ballot is a powerful symbol of political agency, an affirmation of one's stake in society and the collective future. It is an exercise of a right hard-won by generations who understood that the health of a democracy is measured not only by the freedoms it grants but also by the extent to which its citizens are willing to involve themselves in its upkeep.

To appreciate the importance of civic participation, one must first acknowledge that a democracy thrives on the active involvement of its citizens. It is not a spectator sport where the audience passively watches as events unfold; it is, rather, an interactive drama where each citizen is both audience and actor. Civic participation encompasses a broad array of activities including voting, attending community meetings, engaging in public debate, volunteering, serving on local boards, and participating in civic education. These activities serve as the connective tissue between the individual and the broader community, allowing for a continuous exchange of ideas, concerns, and aspirations. Through participation, citizens can influence public policies, hold elected officials accountable, and ensure that their diverse voices are heard. In communities where civic participation is robust, one often finds more effective governance, because officials are more attuned to the needs and wants of their constituents.

Voting, a subset of civic participation, is the cornerstone of democratic governance. It is the mechanism by which the populace exerts direct influence over who will represent them and the policies that will govern their lives. Each vote is an expression of hope, an articulation of values, and a declaration of priorities. By voting, individuals help to legitimize the political system, reinforcing its credibility and stability. When people choose not to vote, they cede their power to those who do, potentially skewing representation and policy outcomes. Low voter turnout can lead to a government that does not reflect the will of the entire populace, undermining the very principle of government "by the people."

Moreover, voting is not just an individual act; it is a communal one that solidifies the social contract. Individuals vote not only for their personal benefit but also for the welfare of the society at large. In casting a ballot, one participates in a collective decision-making process that shapes the community's future. This is especially pertinent in local elections, where the outcomes can have immediate and tangible effects on everyday life, such as education, public safety, and infrastructure. By voting in these local contests, citizens ensure that their community's unique needs and preferences are addressed.

The importance of civic participation and voting also extends to the realm of social equity. Historically, many groups were denied the right to vote and excluded from political processes. Through tireless advocacy and struggle, these rights have been secured for most, yet the battle for full participation continues. Civic participation and voting are tools that can be used to dismantle systemic barriers and promote a more inclusive society. When marginalized groups engage in the political process, they assert their presence and push for policies that address their concerns.

Furthermore, civic participation and voting are acts of education. They require individuals to inform themselves about the issues, the candidates, and the implications of various policy proposals. This process of self-education strengthens the fabric of democracy by creating a more knowledgeable citizenry equipped to make reasoned decisions. In turn, a well-informed electorate is less vulnerable to manipulation and better able to discern the truth from political rhetoric.

The Influence of Virtual Reality on Spatial Awareness and Design

Virtual reality is an emerging technology that has been gaining popularity in recent years. Its ability to simulate real-life environments and experiences has made it a valuable tool in various fields, including education, entertainment, and even healthcare. One of the areas where virtual reality has shown promise is in its impact on spatial awareness and design.

Spatial awareness refers to an individual's ability to understand and navigate their environment, including their perception of space and distance. It is a crucial skill in various fields, such as architecture, engineering, and even gaming. Design, on the other hand, involves the creation of plans and products that meet specific needs and requirements.

The use of virtual reality in architecture and design has been increasing over time. Architects can use VR to create immersive 3D models of their designs, allowing clients to visualize and experience the space before construction begins. This not only saves time and resources but also helps avoid misunderstandings and miscommunications. For instance, a client may have difficulty envisioning how a room will look or feel based on a 2D blueprint; however, with a virtual reality model, they can walk around and interact with the space as if it were real.

Similarly, designers can use VR to test out their ideas and designs in a virtual environment before actually creating the product. This allows them to identify potential flaws or issues early on, saving time and resources in the long run. For example, a furniture designer can test out different arrangements and layouts of a room using VR, ensuring that the final product is functional and aesthetically pleasing.

Moreover, virtual reality has been shown to improve spatial awareness and cognitive skills in individuals. Studies have shown that people who use VR to navigate through virtual environments exhibit better spatial awareness and memory than those who do not. This is because VR requires individuals to engage with their surroundings on a deeper level, leading to improved cognitive function and spatial perception.

In conclusion, virtual reality has had a significant influence on spatial awareness and design. Its ability to simulate real-life environments and experiences has made it a valuable tool for architects, designers, and educators. Additionally, virtual reality has been shown to improve spatial awareness and cognitive skills in individuals. As this technology continues to evolve, its potential applications in various fields will only continue to grow.

Terrorism: The War on Iraq Essay

The war against Iraq by the US has come under a lot of criticism because of the effects it has subjected to the Iraqis and US citizens. The war started on March 2003 during the reign of President George Bush. It is said that the war was planned in early 2002. The war erupted in the name of combating terrorism, but it later turned out that terrorism was just a hidden reason to waste tax payers’ money.

Prior to the war, there were allegations that Iraq was in possession of weapons of mass destructions. Consequently, Saddam Hussein was thought to be collaborating with Al Qaeda to stage terror attacks against US. The UN recommended that Iraq be investigated to find out whether these accusations were true, and indeed there was no evidence to support these accusations (Galbraith 34).

It seems there was bad relationship between Saddam Hussein and the then US president George W. Bush because no one expected him to rage war against Iraq after the UN had confirmed that there were no such weapons in Iraq.

It is certain that president Bush was completing the war that his father had started back in 1991. Besides, the action of the US and Britain to go against the will of UN revealed that the two countries are dominant over the body and one is left to wonder what would have happened if the violation was done by a third world country.

To the ordinary citizens of US, the war was not necessary because it was already costing them millions of money. In addition, there was nothing to be gained from the war apart from inflation because the government was directing most of its funds towards the war. In fact, the invasion made the situation in Iraq to worsen and most people felt that Iraq should have been left to solve its own domestic problems.

To the Americans, the war was unexpected, considering that the national debt has continued to rise to several trillions over the years and yet the money is not being put into good use.

Schell argues that the US war in Iraq caused many innocent people to die. It is not only the Iraqis who died, but also the US military officers (1). This outcome did not mean anything to President Bush because his main objective was to get rid of Saddam Hussein; in fact, the September eleventh attacks gave him a good reason to attack Iraq.

It is true that the people of Iraq were suffering because of the evils committed by their political leader, but even so no one should have died. Bush’s administration thought that by removing Saddam from power they would solve the problems of Iraq.

The outcome was completely opposite because the ethnic communities started to fight each other in an unprecedented scale – women were raped along with their children. The fighting resulted in a humanitarian crisis because the health care providers were overwhelmed by the increased number of patients.

Initially, both the Sunni and the Shiite Muslims were attacking US military, but later on they started to fight amongst themselves. President Bush then requested the military to hang on for some time until the situation became calm. This was just an excuse of exercising control over Iraq. The outcomes of the war suggest that US had not prepared to handle the consequences that would follow after the attack. There was no need of starting a mission that could not be finished.

In this regard, the US should have considered using other approaches in solving the problems in Iraq. This is because the use of force led to destruction of infrastructure and private properties. It cost US a lot of money to rebuild the damaged facilities which was expressed by many as wastage of money that would have been put into good use.

This is because there are so many problems in the US and the citizens expected the government to give its own citizens the first priority instead of focusing on other people’s problems. For instance, by the time the invasion was taking place the rate of unemployment in the US was still high and the nine billion should have been used to help such people to start their own businesses, which in future would increase government revenue through tax collection.

From a legal perspective, the US had no right to attack Iraq and thus if the legal procedures were followed the US could be sued at the international court and a hefty fine would then be imposed. The invasion further interfered with economic activities such as the sale of oil products, which forms the back borne of Iraq’s economy.

This in itself created an impression that the US oppresses developing nations and is selfish because it is only concerned about safeguarding its own interests. This attitude has destroyed the relationship between Islamic nations in the Middle East and the Americans. This is because the invasion was expressed as an attack against Muslims and the Americans too think that all Muslims are terrorists (Galbraith 20).

The attack on Iraq was therefore biased because terrorists are in many parts of the world and if indeed Bush was committed towards ending terrorism, he would have commissioned the apprehension of terrorists in other parts of the world.

Walter reckons that the idea of withdrawing military presence from Iraq should have been implemented earlier instead of waiting until when the situation has worsened (1). The American people do not deserve to face the economic hardships they experienced in the name of fighting terrorism because when they pay taxes to the government they expect that money to be incorporated into the states development projects.

In essence, were it not for the congress, the war on Iraq would not have ended. Prior to the invasion, the US was warned against carrying out the attack, but Bush and his allies chose to ignore that counsel. Most people blame the congress for not preventing the attack because Bush could not have proceeded without authority from the congress.

Bush’s administration was certain that it could restructure Iraq once the invasion was over and they did not think that the cost could accumulate to several billions. Furthermore, they expected full backing from the citizens of Iraq, but this was not the case because the civilians became hostile to US’s presence.

One thing that Bush’s administration did not know is that even if the US is powerful it cannot assume the role of a global policeman, and doing so will cause it to fail in other essential areas. For instance, the rate of crime in US is still high and the government should have given such an issue the first priority because when terrorists prepare to launch attacks they collaborate with local criminals.

The war on terrorism would have been won if only the government would have considered preparing US’s security agents to handle terror attacks. This would have cost less money compared to the huge amounts that was spent in Iraq. Likewise, as the US concentrated on Iraq, terrorist groups in other parts of the world were still executing their plans.

The US invasion on Iraq was meant to exhibit the abilities of the government in fighting terrorism, but contrary to the government’s expectations, the invasion unveiled the incompetence of the US intelligence because all its allegations turned out to be lies. In addition, the invasion failed to bring democracy in Iraq because the continued invasion caused the Iraqis to be split along their ethnic lines.

Thus, the invasion on Iraq has tainted the US’s integrity because in as much as it claimed its main objective was to bring democracy in Iraq by the year 2008, its focus had shifted to helping the Iraqis fight amongst themselves. This created an impression that US leads double standards because if the presence of US military was meant to restore peace it should have maintained a neutral stand without taking sides.

In light of this, the predecessors of President Bush, including Barrack Obama have a long way in restoring back the respect that was once accorded to the US. Bush was misguided into thinking that power is determined by military abilities. This is wrong because for the world to respect someone they consider how he/she make decisions and how he/she interacts with the rest of the world.

Actually, the first challenge that president Obama encountered entailed recalling the military from Iraq. The failure in Iraq’s attack is owed to the politicking that was allowed to take center-stage because if Bush’s administration would have analyzed the positive and the negative side, the government would have identified early indicators of failure and thus, take an affirmative action.

Perhaps, on May 2, 2011, Obama made a leap in the war against terror by announcing the killing of al-Quada leader, Osama bin Laden. However, such developments still raise questions on the possibility of succeeding in war against terror; it is apparent that people around the world, particularly the US are more threatened than before.

In conclusion, the government should consider removing the intelligence officers who misguided the government so that such a mistake does not recur again in future. It is recommended that the government should analyze criticisms because even though it is not what we want to hear it helps us to identify the faults in our decisions.

Therefore, the war on Iraq is not worth the money the US spends yearly. Future presidents should not be allowed to use their influence to solve their personal flaws with other people at the expense of their subjects. The US government should stay away from other countries affairs and let them solve their own problems because if it focuses on other countries problems when will it solve its own problems.

Jazz music has had a profound impact on society since its inception in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It is a unique genre that combines elements of African and European music, resulting in a sound that is both innovative and groundbreaking. Jazz has had a significant impact on American culture and society, influencing everything from art and literature to politics and social issues.

One of the most significant impacts of jazz music on society is its role in the civil rights movement. Jazz musicians were at the forefront of the fight for equality, using their music to express their feelings about the injustices they faced. Jazz clubs were often the only places where black and white people could socialize together, and musicians like Louis Armstrong and Duke Ellington were able to use their fame to advocate for civil rights.

Jazz music also had a significant impact on the art world. The improvisational nature of jazz allowed artists to experiment with new styles and techniques, resulting in a revolution in the world of art. The abstract expressionist movement, which emerged in the 1940s and 1950s, was heavily influenced by jazz music and the freedom it represented.

Literature was also influenced by jazz music, with writers like Ernest Hemingway and Gertrude Stein using jazz as a theme in their works. The bebop movement of the 1940s, which featured complex chord progressions and rapid-fire drumming, inspired writers to experiment with new forms of language and structure.

Jazz music has also had a significant impact on politics and social issues. Jazz musicians were often at the forefront of the fight against oppression, using their music to express their feelings about the injustices they faced. Jazz clubs were often the only places where black and white people could socialize together, and musicians like Louis Armstrong and Duke Ellington were able to use their fame to advocate for civil rights.

Jazz music has also had a significant impact on fashion and style. The jazz age, which lasted from the 1920s to the 1940s, was a time of great social and cultural change, and jazz music was at the center of it all. Fashion during this time was characterized by loose fitting clothing and bold, bright colors, reflecting the energy and excitement of the jazz scene.

In conclusion, jazz music has had a profound impact on society, influencing everything from art and literature to politics and social issues. Its unique blend of African and European music has resulted in a sound that is both innovative and groundbreaking, and its impact on American culture and society cannot be overstated. Jazz music has been a force for change throughout its history, and its influence continues to be felt today.

Euthanasia: Advantages and Disadvantages Essay

Table of Contents
 1. Introduction
 2. Euthanasia- Pros and Cons
 3. Conclusion
 4. Works Cited

Introduction

Euthanasia, or as it’s known in English as ‘mercy killing’, is a Greek term for ‘good death’ and has been one of the most controversial and heatedly debated topics in healthcare and politics. It’s an intentionally administered death to a patient of a fatal injury or disease and is administered with the consent of the patient/victim and their relatives, although there have been cases where it has been done without consent. It’s a controversial policy topic for policymakers, politicians, lawyers, and the medical community and has been legalized in several states of the USA, whereas in many states, it remains violently protested against the notion and has been tagged as physician-assisted suicide. (Burke J. Balch, 2006). There are many aspects of euthanasia, with voluntary euthanasia being on the request of the patient and involuntary where no such request is made and no consent is asked for (or given). For patients undergoing severe medical treatments, the withdrawal of medical facilities and thus leaving them vulnerable to death is euthanasia by omission (i.e. omission of medical aids or life-saving facilities). For other patients suffering from incurable diseases, the administering of fatal, venomous injections to give them a slow (albeit painless) death is called euthanasia by action.

Euthanasia- Pros and Cons

There have been numerous and many intense debates for and against euthanasia, with equal merit on both sides and pro – euthanasia thinkers being called merciless and those lacking faith and other Godly considerations. The most popular arguments against euthanasia include the derogation of human life and disregard for an individual’s right to live. The most heavily criticized of all such similar actions is involuntary euthanasia which bears the brunt of all severe protests against the issue, with involuntary euthanasia being dubbed as the deprivation of an individual of their basic right to live and die fully. This is the notion most historians and policymakers of all states banning it holds. They regard the whole necessity of choosing one’s death by the state laws as a request to let the government sell contaminated food to its citizens knowing it’s harmful to their health. The slippery slope phenomenon is also a famous theory against the question of legalizing euthanasia, ascertaining that the practice might be extended to people who are terminally ill to people who could be saved otherwise but eat up a lot of resources which makes it open to economic considerations as opposed to ethical/human ones. Another stand very popular among the medical community is that the crucial healthcare rule is the will to health and quality life and the abstinence of willing anything which may prove detrimental to an individual (Robinson, 2007).

The pros on the other hand provide quite interesting perspectives on the issue. Proponents can give almost every counter-statement to everything the opponents have to say to vilify the practice of euthanasia. The basic of all healthcare intentions is to relieve the sufferer’s suffering. This is should entail putting an end to the pain and torture of perpetual illness by administering peaceful death. This also follows a basic question of freedom of choice, everyone should have the right to choose for themselves, their life and death, and the government should not interfere in such crucial and personal decisions (ProCon.org, 2009).

Conclusion

Looking at both sides introduces some personal concerns in the mind regarding whether one should be given the right to live and die or not. Both above such abstract and seemingly complex considerations is one more objective and more critical factor that needs to be taken into account while deciding the fate of euthanasia and policies regarding its legality.

Looking at the issue from a governmental and economical perspective, facilities administered to terminally ill patients are usually very expensive and exhaust the already scarce resources at hand. So even if deliberately putting an end to a patient who’s already proceeding slowly toward a painful, hopeless end might seem selfish and hurried, it’s wise to sometimes give up such considerations in regard for the ‘greater good that can come out of such decisions. It’s rather important to free up r4esouces for people who have hope of recovery and need them to lead better lives as opposed to people who’re immune to all cures and expensive treatments and end up becoming a burden to society.

 3. Robinson, B. (2007). euthanasia and physician assisted suicide.

Once upon a time, when philosophers wondered about the essence of existence, they were particularly curious about consciousness. They pondered the very nature of our awareness, perception, and thoughts. It was a complex and mysterious subject that has fascinated many minds throughout history. As the world evolved, science started to delve into the depths of consciousness and its role in our lives.

One day, a scientist named Alan Turing proposed a test to determine the level of consciousness in artificial intelligence. He believed that if a machine could exhibit the characteristics of a human being, it could be considered conscious. The Turing Test was a turning point that sparked intense debates regarding the nature of consciousness and its implications for Artificial Intelligence (AI).

Nowadays, the philosophical discourse on consciousness has expanded to include not only human beings but also other living organisms, animals, and even machines. The idea is that consciousness might not be limited to humans but could potentially be a universal trait shared by many entities. This broader understanding of consciousness has led to the development of various theories, each offering different perspectives on the essence of consciousness.

One prominent theory is the 'Functionalist' approach, which suggests that consciousness can be defined by its function rather than its substance. According to this view, consciousness is not a single, unified entity, but rather a complex and dynamic system that arises from the interaction of various brain processes. These processes can be observed, analyzed, and potentially emulated by machines, leading to the possibility of constructing conscious machines. The Functionalist approach has been influential in shaping the field of AI, as it encourages the pursuit of creating intelligent machines that can exhibit conscious-like behaviors.

On the other hand, some philosophers argue that consciousness is a fundamentally distinct and unique aspect of life, not reducible to mere functions or interactions. They believe that consciousness is a mysterious quality that transcends the material world, and thus it cannot be replicated in a machine. This perspective is often referred to as the 'Emergentist' or 'Non-Reductionist' approach, and it challenges the idea that AI can ever truly possess consciousness.

As the debate on the nature of consciousness rages on, the implications for Artificial Intelligence become increasingly significant. If consciousness can be viewed as a function or an emergent property, then it could potentially be replicated within machines, leading to the development of more advanced and intelligent AI. This could have profound consequences for various fields, including medicine, education, and even the military.

However, if consciousness remains an ineffable and unique feature of living organisms, then the pursuit of AI may never fully realize its full potential. This would limit the scope of AI's influence and prevent it from truly revolutionizing the world as we know it.

Regardless of the stance one takes on the nature of consciousness, it is evident that the philosophy of consciousness holds great importance for the future of Artificial Intelligence. Whether AI can ever possess consciousness or not, it is crucial to continue exploring the depths of consciousness and its implications for the ever-evolving world of technology.
