Urban agriculture is a growing trend that is taking root in cities around the world. As urban populations continue to grow, there is a growing need for sustainable and efficient ways to feed the city dwellers of the future. Urban agriculture offers a unique solution to this problem by utilizing small plots of land, often in underutilized urban spaces, to grow fresh produce and other foods that can be used to feed city residents. By embracing urban agriculture, cities can not only ensure that their residents have access to fresh, healthy food, but can also improve their environmental sustainability, reduce their carbon footprint, and provide a unique opportunity for community engagement and education.
One of the most significant benefits of urban agriculture is that it can help to increase access to fresh, healthy food in areas where it is often difficult to find. In many cities, residents living in inner-city neighborhoods or low-income areas often have limited access to fresh produce and other healthy foods. This can lead to poor diets, health problems, and a lack of awareness about nutrition and healthy eating habits. By growing food in urban spaces, cities can help to provide fresh, locally grown produce to residents who may not otherwise have access to it.
Another benefit of urban agriculture is that it can help to improve environmental sustainability. By growing food in urban spaces, cities can reduce the amount of energy and resources needed to transport food from rural farms to urban markets. This can help to reduce the carbon footprint of the food system and promote the use of sustainable farming practices. Additionally, urban agriculture can help to reduce the amount of waste that ends up in landfills by recycling organic waste and using it to grow food.
Urban agriculture also provides a unique opportunity for community engagement and education. By growing food in urban spaces, cities can provide a platform for community members to come together and learn about food production, nutrition, and sustainability. This can help to promote a greater understanding of the food system and encourage healthier eating habits. Additionally, urban agriculture can provide a valuable learning opportunity for students, who can learn about farming and food production in a hands-on setting.
In conclusion, urban agriculture is an important tool for feeding cities of the future and promoting sustainability, community engagement, and education. By embracing this growing trend, cities can help to ensure that their residents have access to fresh, healthy food, while also improving their environmental sustainability and promoting a greater understanding of the food system. With the growing demand for fresh, locally grown produce, it is clear that urban agriculture will continue to play an important role in feeding the cities of the future.

Introduction 

The formation of an individual's character is influenced by numerous variables both within and outside their control. These elements have a profound impact on how people think, behave, make judgments, and interact with others. Internal causes such as personal choices, motives, and beliefs are equally important to external factors including peer pressure, social norms, and mass media. This essay will analyze these various factors and their effects on one's personality, exploring how they shape our identities, attitudes, behaviors, and life paths.  

Internal Factors Shaping Character  
Personal Decision-Making Processes  A person's sense of self emerges from the inside out via their own decision-making processes. One's set of principles guides them through life, helping them distinguish between what is right and wrong for them and allowing them to act accordingly. An individual's moral compass may originate from religious ideologies, upbringing, education, or personal experiences. For instance, if someone has had negative interactions with alcoholic family members, they might choose abstinence as a way to honor their loved ones while protecting themselves. Their value system shapes their behavior when faced with situations involving drugs and alcohol.   

Goals & Motivation  Goals serve as pivotal drivers of human progress, fueling ambition across every arena of existence; whether professional endeavors or interpersonal relationships - we strive towards objectives which inspire us toward meaningful achievements. Ambition fuels determination but also presents potential pitfalls if pursued blindly without considering consequences or ethical considerations. Setting realistic yet challenging aspirations allows individuals to grow, learn from failures, develop resilience against hardships, and find fulfillment along their journey.    

Self-Esteem & Self-Confidence  Our perception of ourselves greatly affects our actions and emotions. People with strong self-esteem tend to feel more confident expressing opinions, taking risks, forming connections, and adapting to new circumstances. On the other hand, low self-esteem can hinder growth by causing apprehension about trying novel activities or speaking up in group settings - leading to missed opportunities and unrealized potential. Thus, developing healthy levels of confidence throughout childhood helps establish resilient foundations upon which adult lives can flourish later down the line.     

External Elements Impacting Personality Formation  
Peer Pressure  Peer groups play significant roles in shaping who we become due to the influence exerted by its members' expectations, behaviors, preferences, and attitudes. As adolescents spend most waking hours surrounded by same-aged peers at home or school, they often conform to fit into accepted standards defined by their social circles. This phenomenon can lead young minds away from unique expressions of identity development and onto predetermined routes deemed acceptable by popular opinion - sometimes resulting in suppressed originality.  

Social Media Influence  Social networking sites like Instagram offer idealized glimpses into "perfect" lifestyles crafted intentionally by users seeking validation or attention from followers. Users frequently compare their seemingly ordinary lives unfavorably to these curated highlight reels - feeling deficient or inadequate because reality does not measure up to societal beauty standards or material possessions showcased online. Such constant exposure erodes body image stability among youths, further perpetuating insecurities rooted deep within each individual.  

Parental Guidance  Parental involvement significantly shapes children's developmental trajectories as parents provide fundamental lessons regarding appropriate conduct and morality before entering formal educational institutions where additional guidance is offered. Positive parenting techniques stress empathy, honesty, responsibility, respect, boundaries, open communication channels, conflict resolution strategies, and balanced discipline methods that emphasize natural consequence rather than punishment alone. All these components combined create safe environments conducive for thriving during formative years thereby influencing long term character traits of offspring as they mature into independent adults capable making sound decisions based on learned behaviors and core values instilled early on.  

Media Representation  Popular culture portrayals typically feature stereotypical characters reinforcing limiting gender roles, prejudices, and racial biases that deeply embed harmful ideas into impressionable psyches. Passive consumption can desensitize viewers, normalizing problematic attitudes towards marginalized communities. Active engagement with diverse forms of entertainment provides alternative perspectives essential for fostering acceptance and understanding among all backgrounds. By consuming media responsibly, audiences can challenge oppressive narratives promoting inclusivity and equality.  

Teacher Effectiveness  Teachers play pivotal roles in cultivating future leaders equipped with critical thinking skills necessary for success post-graduation. High quality educators possess qualities like empathy, enthusiasm, expertise, flexibility, warmth and authenticity; all hallmarks of effective teaching styles that resonate positively with students’ needs allowing them to flourish academically as well as personally. When teachers genuinely invest time nurturing each student individually - beyond mere academic goals - they empower young minds with essential tools needed navigate lifelong learning journeys successfully.  

Conclusion 
Character is formed by a complex web of internal and external forces that shape our thoughts, feelings, actions, and destinies. Recognizing the significance of both intrinsic and extrinsic factors enables us to make intentional decisions that align with our values and contribute to personal growth. Embracing diversity and inclusivity allows everyone access to resources supporting positive change - breaking cycles of negativity and fostering strengthened bonds within communities worldwide. Ultimately, embarking on this journey requires courageous introspection and mindfulness so we may better understand ourselves and others around us - creating brighter futures together.

Project Reset and the Domestic Violence Court Dissertation

After a thorough examination of the existing criminal justice policies, I concluded that the most promising programs relate to the issues of youth domestic violence and young adult (16-17-years-old) criminals ( Operating programs , n.d.). I consider these programs to be the most promising because they address the issues of youth that are relevant to the US community. Young adult criminals’ delinquencies are currently addressed by the Project Reset. This program allows the youngsters to evade the adverse consequences of a criminal record and is considered to be an invigorating substitute for criminal court practices ( Operating programs , n.d.). The Domestic Violence Court is another program aimed at the mitigation of negative outcomes in teens. This initiative fully addresses domestic violence cases where 16-19-year-old individuals are involved in any kind of domestic violence manifestation ( Operating programs , n.d.). This court features a dedicated justice of the peace that has to deal with the exceptional requests made by teens in the court.

These two programs have a serious impact on the way that juvenile justice and the police view young adults and their standing in society. The majority of the decisions in courts are aimed to mitigate the effects of the strict criminal justice system of the United States. All of the parts of the legal system (including the law enforcement agency) should comply with the keystones of these two programs and do everything to certify the successful implementation of this program. Moreover, juvenile justice essentials and the correction procedures may be dynamically amended by the legal and social needs of the programs (Shoemaker, 2013). This is one of the biggest advantages of these programs because it allows the court to plan the funding of these initiatives in an efficient manner.

The initiatives are funded based on government budget priorities. The courts tend to choose from two popular options – grants from the Department of Justice and local funding opportunities. The courts may also seek federal funding. For the most part, courts depend on federal block grants, and the support coming from the Department of Justice is irreplaceable. The commitment to the project can be signified by local funding. The budget will be allocated in a way that would allow the government to cover the basic needs of the programs and utilize reserve resources is additional expenditures are inevitable (Marion & Oliver, 2012). Because the programs linked to youth are considered to be of pivotal importance, it is safe to say that governmental decisions concerning the budget opportunities are well-thought-out and effectively address the needs of the US citizens.

The criminal justice reform depends on the revisions of the US criminal justice policies conducted by the court. The impact of the court on the criminal justice policies can be explained by the major cost cuts triggered by the initiatives passed by the courts. In other words, the decisions made by the courts across the country allowed to improve public safety while decreasing the costs of the latter (Gaines, 2014). Taking into account the fact that court funding continues to diminish slowly, the courts’ initiatives can be called redeemable. The overall state of affairs proves that the courts are directly involved in the process of the development of new criminal justice policies, and the decisions made by the court are thoroughly discussed by the US legal apparatus.

Writing a 1000-Word Essay: Sticking to Limits Essay (Article)

Instructors often place restrictions on the number of words that students can write in an assignment. This may create difficulties for students who may have too many ideas on the concerned topics. However, others may feel that this is a positive attribute as it allows them to focus on specific issues.

Quick pointers on 1000-word essays

Give the essay adequate time – Students must realize that no matter how simple the topic may be adequate time allocation is a definite necessity. Sometimes one may imagine that the essay will take two hours only to find that it has dragged on for four hours or more. When minimal time is given to the task, this often compromises on the quality of the essay.

Organize your ideas – a 1000-word essay may often turn out to be four pages long if common fonts have been used. Therefore, students must take the time to prepare a draft of what they want to include in the piece. One should reflect on the main idea and the arguments that support those main ideas. The paper must end with a conclusion that can be linked to the main idea. Formatting and rewriting the 1000-word essay may be necessary in order to eliminate possible problems.

Be careful with the grammar – No matter what topic or course a student is associated with, one must never compromise on the quality of grammar used in one’s essay. Grammatical constructions should be used to link concepts in the work and the use of passive voice should be avoided.

I hated dinner parties, and I hated even more that they were mandatory. There were only a handful of us "time travelers" and it was no secret that I had the most boring, useless, and uneventful time slot to play in. Everyone else would be bragging of great battles they rigged, the technological advancements they made, or the faith and religions they were spreading to their people. As for me, well you can only watch so many natural disasters before they become mundane. I walked into the dining room of Cody's house, where all our dinner parties are held, and put on a fake smile. "Hey! Frank's here!" said a man from across the room, gesturing me to come over and socialize. There were two other people standing there with the man who called to me when I walked into the room. "Hello, Shane." I said to the man. "Coleen, Michael." I said, smiling at the other two people standing with Shane. "Guess what I did today, Frank." said Coleen, wasting no time in taunting me that her playground was better than mine. "I invented the telephone." she finished before I could answer. " Alexander Graham Bell invented the telephone, Coleen." Michael said. Everything was a competition with these guys. "Of course he did." countered Coleen. "But who do you think laid the foundation to get him there?" she winked at Michael and popped an hors d'oeuvre into her mouth. "That's nothing. Michael, tell Frank what you did today!" said Shane, smiling. "Nah, it's not a big deal." said Michael. I knew he was lying. He couldn't wait to tell me. "Stop being modest, tell him!" Frank encouraged him. "Alright, alright. I've been working on this for a few years now, but I finally made it happen. I started the Great Crusades today. I almost gave up on it, but all I had to do was dress myself up as a priest, convince then I could talk to god, and tell them to kill everyone. It was quite simple, I gave them too much credit." I rolled my eyes, I didn't really get the appeal of tricking people into slaughtering each other. Shane noticed I was unimpressed with Michael's story. "So what did you do today, Frank?" He asked. "I don't want to bore you, I can assure you it's not as exciting as what you guys did today." I countered sarcastically, while Michael smiled and Coleen flipped her hair. Shane wasn't letting up, though. "Today is April Fool's Day, Frank. I know you did something, you'd never miss an opportunity to pull a prank." I smiled, Shane was right. I did like a good prank. "You're right, although I did keep it on the smaller side this year." Suddenly I had the attention of my three peers. "Well are you going to tell us or what?" Coleen complained. "Don't get your hopes up." I said "Like I said, it was just something small. I set my coordinates to random and ended up at the Vienna Academy of Fine Arts in the year 1907. After wandering around for a bit I found my way into the Admissions office. Sitting on top of the secretary's desk was an acceptance letter addressed to someone named "Adolf Hitler." Well, I just changed some words around and changed the letter to a rejection letter." When I finished I realized the room had grown silent and everyone was staring at me.

Dear Principal,

I believe that community service is a good deed and that everyone should be required to at least do some kind of community service.

Also, all students should be require to do at least one kind of community service per school year.

For example, they could hold a day where they go around the community and pick up trash.

They could also do something easier like tutor elementary school students.

It doesn't have to be something hard, as long as they affect the community in a positive way.

If the student doesn't do community service at least one time in the school year, then they wouldn't get their final report card until they complete one community service activity.

So that means that their parents are not going to be able to see their report card until they complete it.

If students don't know what kind of community service to do, our school has a community service club where students help the community in a variety of ways.

It is fun because you can meet new people in this club.

Also, you can get to know your community better.

It also helps you to complete one community service by the end of school year.

It is a fun and easy way to complete this task.

To prove that each student did a community service, they would have to have a parent signature on a form that explains and verifies that they completed it.

But if they join the community service club, they would just need to get the club supervisor's signature.

Also they should be required to turn in a reflection about the community service they did with their form so we know what kind of community service they did.

If they don't turn in that form and the reflection by the end of the school year, then they would have to suffer the consequences.

So that is why I strongly believe why all of our students are required to do community service.

It is a good way to help students become better people.

Sincerely,

Student

Position of Women in Islam Essay

Introduction

Islam does not grant equal rights to men and women, as many people wrongly assume. Women are obligated to wear veil, which is seen as the oppressive symbol of a woman’s subservience to men by Western feminism. However, Islamic women proudly assess the veil as the symbol of their identity. Such controversial perception of the women’s position in Islam has resulted in the widespread belief that feminism will never be a part of Muslim society and that Islamic women accept their subordinate status willingly.

Assessment of Women’s Position in Islam

Women living in Islamic environments are expected to be humble, supportive, and silent. There is a clear differentiation of female and male responsibilities and statuses in Islamic society. According to Quran and the Shari’ah, men and women are entitled to separate legal statuses, however, both men and women have been prescribed the right to conduct business and to possess property. If the woman is damaged or harmed, she has the right to demand compensation, just as the man. Islamic traditions allow one man to marry more than one woman, and while many non-Muslim marks this practice as unethical, Islamic women do not regard it as a threat. The law requires Islamic women to wear the veil, not to show their face or body to anybody except for the husband, even though not a single Islamic woman would note that this tradition is oppressive. On the contrary, Islamic women are confident that the veil signified their rejection of the modern value system, while Islam elevates women to the position of respect and honor. The law of Islam does not allow contraception, abortions, and marriage on a female’s choice. However, on the other side, Islamic women do not consider their position as inferior or required by traditions; they are willing to follow these laws. Therefore, their position should be assessed as welcomed by Islamic women themselves.

Conclusion

The position of women in Islam is hard to understand from a Western perspective. American or European woman is unlikely to support the lifestyle of the average woman living in accordance with the Islamic rules. Nevertheless, Islamic women enjoy a wide range of rights equal to men, including the right to conduct business and own property. The key point is that Islamic women are satisfied with their status and believe that Quran protects their rights more than any other law in the western communities.

Introduction:

The topic of animal rights has been debated for many years, with varying opinions on the treatment of animals, particularly in the context of animal experimentation. Animal experimentation refers to the use of animals in scientific research and training to gain knowledge, develop new treatments, and improve human and animal health. This practice has been a contentious issue, particularly due to the potential suffering and death of animals involved in these experiments. This essay will discuss the various ethical considerations related to animal rights in animal experimentation for research and training.

Animal Rights and the Moral Status of Animals:

The moral status of animals has been a long-standing debate, with some arguing that animals have the same rights as humans, while others believe they should not be given the same level of protection. Animal rights advocates argue that animals are sentient beings capable of experiencing pain and suffering, and as such, they should be protected from unnecessary harm. They also contend that animals have inherent value, and their lives should not be subjected to human interests without proper consideration of the animals' well-being.

Conversely, those who oppose animal rights maintain that animals lack the same level of moral value as humans and that their primary purpose is to serve human needs. They argue that animals, particularly those in agricultural and scientific settings, are bred for specific purposes, and their lives are already predetermined to serve human interests.

Ethical Considerations in Animal Experimentation:

The use of animals in research and training raises several moral issues, primarily in determining when and how animal experimentation is justified. One of the primary considerations in this debate is the potential for animal suffering and the extent to which it should be minimized. Proponents of animal experimentation argue that the potential benefits to human and animal health outweigh the suffering experienced by animals. They also note that advances in animal care, such as anesthesia and pain relief, have led to a decrease in animal suffering during experiments.

However, opponents of animal experimentation argue that the potential benefits are often overstated, and that the suffering experienced by animals is not justified. They also assert that the potential for human error and the possibility of harm to the animal outweigh the potential benefits of the experiment.

Alternative Methods:

In recent years, there has been a growing emphasis on alternative methods to animal experimentation, such as in vitro studies, computer modeling, and the use of alternative animal models. These methods have the potential to reduce animal suffering and provide a more reliable method of research.

However, critics argue that these methods have limitations and may not fully replicate the complex physiological processes that occur in living organisms. Additionally, these alternative methods can be expensive and time-consuming, making them less feasible for some researchers.

Conclusion:

The debate surrounding animal experimentation for research and training is complex and multifaceted. While animal experimentation has led to significant advances in human and animal health, the potential for harm to animals cannot be ignored. As such, it is essential to consider the ethical considerations surrounding animal experimentation, including the potential for animal suffering, the potential benefits of the research, and the availability of alternative methods. By carefully weighing these factors, researchers can make informed decisions about the use of animals in research and training, ultimately minimizing harm to animals while maximizing the potential benefits of their work.

Analysis of King Khalid Foundation Essay

Table of Contents
 1. Introduction
 2. Organization’s History
 3. Beneficiaries
 4. Scope
 5. Reporting
 6. Resources Provided
 7. Conclusion
 8. References

Introduction

King Khalid Foundation (KKF) is a non-profit organization based in Saudi Arabia. According to Arab Foundation’s Forum (2012), this foundation operates towards improving the social and economic status of citizens of Saudi Arabia. This organization bears the idea that people can bring change to their own lives if they are guided and empowered towards set goals and objectives.

King Khalid Foundation (n.d.), highlights that this organization is involved in a number of activities: funding community development projects, providing emergency relief services, conducting and also publishing research and awarding other non-profit organizations, corporations and individuals who have achieved much towards social and economic growth within Saudi Arabia.

The foundation as non-government organization has the following mission: “to always use their resources and knowledge for the sake of positive impact in people’s life with a result of providing solutions to both social and economical problems within Saudi Arabia” (King Khalid Foundation, n.d., p. 1).

Organization’s History

According to Interactive Saudi Arabia (2010), King Khalid Foundation was established in 2001 after King Khalid’s death. It was established by his family members in his remembrance. King Khalid had ruled Saudi Arabia from 1975 to 1982; his regime came to an end as he died in 1982. This organization is controlled by several people: nine board of trustees and 11 members.

The board of trustee leads this organization and it is responsible of making policies in which the organization follows to achieve their set objectives. Its main aim is to lead people in achievement of better social and economic production through engaging themselves in activities that would enable the citizens towards realizing their vision. According to Saudi Arabia Competitiveness Index (2008), King Khalid Foundation has a vision of strengthening and encouraging community and organization development work in Saud Arabia; this is to improve the lives of the citizens

Beneficiaries

King Khalid Foundation is devoted in training non profit organization leaders to acquire knowledge that can later be disseminated to the community in their programmes, hence resulting to high production in the society. They offer funds directed to capacity building trainings, partnership-building and resource mobilization, database management, coaching and consulting areas. All these areas are administered to the leaders in non-profit organizations in Saudi Arabia (King Khalid Foundation, n.d.).

According to Columbia Business School (2008), King Khalid Foundations funds Columbia University to offer courses related to non-profit management, leading senior team, strategic analysis, decision making and resource allocation. This is meant for equipping leaders from all the Saudi Arabia’s non-profit organizations and business people.

Its main aim is to empower them with the relevant skills and knowledge that is necessary in serving the citizens and building their capacity towards self reliance (Columbia Business School, 2008).

The key areas that King Khalid Foundation is much concerned with while funding Columbia Business School are situational and strategic analysis which includes how to cope-up with any eventuality that may arise in the organization, fundamentals of non-profit management, decision making, negotiating effectively, managing change, acquiring and allocation of resources which involves; how to write quality proposals that can qualify for funding (Columbia Business School, 2008).

The goal of this program is significant: “get knowledge on how to allocate financial resources effectively, understanding the skills to take an organization through effective change, apply key ideas meant for organizational management, enhance leadership skills and be aware of how to deal with conflicts” (Columbia Business School, 2008, p. 1). Through these programs, the leaders benefit with the knowledge and in the long run the citizens benefit through the services such non-profit organizations provide.

Through awarding of business people who have shown outstanding achievement, people in the business arena benefits from this foundation. According to Saudi Arabia Competitiveness Index (2008), King Khalid Foundation started this program of awarding individuals, non-profit organizations and companies as a way of recognizing their efforts in competing for higher productivity in their field.

This was also meant to motivate people to work hard and the more they put more effort as they compete for the awards the more productive they become. Saudi Arabia Responsible Competitiveness Index (SARCI) is concerned in weighing which individuals, organizations or companies does well and qualify for the awards.

This encourages individuals and companies contributions to the society and acts as a better way of ensuring efficient businesses with great positive impact in the society (Saudi Arabia Competitiveness Index, 2008). Responsible competitiveness was a strategy to ensure that Saudi Arabia becomes one among the 10 competitive economies in the whole world, this is the reason why the government of Saudi Arabia started Saudi Arabia Responsible Competitiveness Index though funded by King Khalid Foundation.

King Khalid Award for Responsible Competitiveness was established in 2009. Every year this program awards three strongest companies and individuals from all areas so long as they qualify for this competition. This award is offered to companies that strengthen dependency between prosperous communities and competitive businesses (Saudi Arabia Responsible Competitiveness Index, 2011). With motivation, individual and companies can compete and achieve a lot in terms of productivity without realizing. This was a recommendable move for King Khalid Foundation and it encourages the working culture among people.

According to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia Ministry of Foreign Affairs (2009), Prince Faisal bin Khalid bin Abdul-Aziz was awarded the King Khalid prize for national achievement in 2009. His achievement in improving higher learning and establishment of university was recognized by the foundation by being awarded the best individual who had worked towards liberating people from ignorance and promoting empowerment.

Such an award to leaders can encourage many more leaders to work hard in the areas that they are entrusted in and at the end they will have worked towards development of the country (Ministry of Foreign Affairs, 2009).

The King Khalid Foundation is also helping the needy people with emergency relief in areas where people are hungry and cannot access medical services. The foundation provides food, water, clothes and other necessities to the vulnerable groups in the country. King Khalid eye specialist Hospital is one of the hospitals that have been set and funded by king Khalid foundation to help the needy that may have eye problems. This is a program that has been set to uplift people’s dignity through provision of the necessities as well as equipping them with the relevant skills that may help them cope with a similar situation in the future in an effective way (King Khalid Foundation, n.d.).

Scope

King Khalid Foundation operates within a limited scope: across the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. It has not extended its services to other nations since it was established as an honour of King Khalid who was a leader in this country and in his legacy the foundation was established. Its focus is on the needy citizens and those who contribute towards high production. According to Acumen Fund (2010), King Khalid foundation has been focusing on assisting the grass root people towards contributing to the socio-economic growth of Saudi Arabia.

As the foundation partners with the Acumen Fund, they enable the needy to get knowledge on how to use logical business mind-set towards solving poverty among people in the society. They are also equipped with knowledge on agriculture, housing, water, health and energy. The reason behind this effort is to empower them to be self reliant and be in a position to limit or avoid some calamities like hunger that may befall them (Acumen Fund, 2010).

Reporting

According to Riyadh (2010), without a strategic framework an organization may not know where it is going, the reason as to why it is operating and the way to reach its set goals. It is with this focus that the foundation has come-up with a strategic planning process which helps it in reporting and accounting for all its activities.

The foundation has come-up with six steps that help it to monitor itself: preparation, assessment, envisioning, creating, implementing and evaluation. These six steps help in reporting since an organization through revisiting what happened in each step it is in a position to communicate to all the stakeholders on what has been done and what has been planned to be done.

The stakeholders who may require the report include: clients, community partners and funding partners (Riyadh, 2010). Through reporting it is possible to determine whether it is delivering to the community or not.

Resources Provided

The foundation provides and contributes a lot to the people of Saudi Arabia. It provides relief food and other emergencies to the needy, funds community development projects and offers awards to companies, corporations and individuals who have outstanding achievement towards the country’s economy.

According to Dossal (n.d.), King Khalid Foundation in partnership with the United Nations office is involved in enhancing the strategies laid in achieving the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs). The foundation therefore, works to help Saudi Arabia citizens realize these development goals and improve their living status.

According to Dossal (2011), the foundation has also been holding forums in preparing people to abandon the traditional and charitable approaches and instead learn how to become independent through involving themselves in small investments. The foundation has been in the fore front on issues related to empowerment of citizens since it advocates for people to be empowered financially.

Conclusion

The King Khalid Foundation has initiated many programs since its inception; it has assisted many people in Saudi Arabia to get education and skills in preparation for higher production in the country. This is a challenge to all other non-profit organizations operating across the world. They need to emulate the foundation and work towards helping the target groups rather than misusing the funds as they are directed to projects that they were never intended to.

The issue of giving awards to the best performers is a good accelerator on the speed of production among people. If this is emulated by other non-profit organizations, it can serve as good way of encouraging people to work more and in return the country’s economy will grow at a higher rate.

A fever is your body deliberately getting hotter. It helps you beat an infection. So it's natural that you feel cold and try and warm up. Then when your body is too hot it makes you sweat to cool down. You might also feel a bit sick and your muscles might ache. Your body temperature can go up to 104F (40C) and more. If you have a high fever your skin might feel hot to the touch. But you can still get a fever if your skin feels cool. So what's the best way to cool down? Take paracetamol, ibuprofen or aspirin. But don't give aspirin to children under 16 because it can make them seriously ill. Cool baths. This sounds the most natural way to get cool. But it can be too much for some people. It can make you shiver and make you feel colder. Sponge yourself down with cool water. Wrap a flannel around a basin of cold water and wring it out. Then sponge your arms, legs and chest. Don't use cold water on your face or stomach because it's too close to your heart. Wear cool clothes. Drink plenty of fluids. Your body needs water to cool down. Stay in bed if you can. If you're worried or your temperature goes above 104F (40C) call your doctor. How do I take a temperature? You can measure your temperature by putting a thermometer in your mouth, under your arm or in your bottom (rectum). If you put the thermometer under your arm the temperature will be lower than your body temperature. So you need to add 1F (0.5C). Putting a thermometer in your bottom is usually the most accurate way to measure a temperature. You can buy a digital thermometer that reads the temperature in about 30 seconds.

Harry Whitlam died after Gary Green, 51, of Bradburn Road, Wakefield, reversed the vehicle into him at Swithens Farm, Rothwell, near Leeds, in August 2013. Leeds Crown Court heard he was more than two times the legal driving limit. The court was told Green must have consumed the equivalent of 13 pints of beer before going to bed at 02:00 BST. Harry's mother Pam Whitlam, who worked at the farm's cafe, said her close-knit family had been "changed forever." "It is not OK for anyone, whether on a public road or private land, to be drunk and get behind the wheel of a vehicle," she said. "My hope today, now the court process is complete, is that Harry's life becomes more than one day and as a family we can again remember the good times we shared." "We all miss him dearly and it has not got easier with time but harder," she added. "Harry was my youngest son, a much-loved brother, grandson, nephew and cousin. "The only memories I currently have of Harry are from the day of the accident but his life was so much more." Green, who was jailed for 16 months and two weeks, had previously admitted failing to ensure the safety of others. He was prosecuted under health and safety legislation rather than road traffic law as he was on private land at the time of Harry's death. During an investigation by the Health and Safety Executive (HSE), inspectors found he had been walking towards a worker in a closed-off area of the farm when Green backed the tractor into him at about 09:15 on 9 August. HSE inspector Julian Franklin said it was "an extremely tragic case" and described Green's behaviour as "reckless."

“Far from the Madding Crowd” Novel by Thomas Hardy Essay

Table of Contents
 1. Introduction
 2. Key Objectives
 3. Conclusion
 4. Work Cited

Introduction

The emotional weight of unrequited love often becomes the central conflict or, at the very least, an important plot point of numerous novels. In Far from Madding Crowd , the entire plot revolves around characters’ feelings being rejected. The stark contrast between the harsh reality and the peaceful setting of the novel makes the realization of rejection particularly striking.

Key Objectives

The novel starts with a strong plot line unraveling the drama between Gabriel Oak and his unrequited feelings for Bathsheba. The longing for emotional connection and the affection that Oak displays becomes evident as he roams in search for his peace of mind and starts working at Bathsheba’s farm to provide emotional support for her. Not wanting to force Bathsheba into returning his feelings, Oak shows the true power of selfishness with his actions (Hardy 21).

Remarkably, Oak is not the only character who experiences the pain of unrequited love. Boldwood also has strong feelings for Bathsheba, yet they are no reciprocated either since she is in love with Sergeant Troy. Ironically, the latter shows no interest in her, thus locking the chain of unhappy coincidences in Far from Madding Crowd . Being quite vocal in her refusal to marry Boldwood, Bathsheba feels increasingly depressed and anxious, with her unreciprocated feelings toward Sergeant Troy aggravating the situation.

Conclusion

Thus, with three characters, whose passion for their loved ones knows no boundaries, and the emotionally frozen Sergeant Troy, Far from Madding Crowd represents a dram that is complex in its simplicity and seemingly mundane nature. As Bathsheba realizes that her love for Troy will never have a happy resolution, she agrees to marry Oak. While seemingly unhappy, the resolution of the novel hints at the possibility of trust-based relationships being more important than passion that may fade away as time passes.

Work Cited

Hardy, Thomas. Far from the Madding Crowd . Modern Library, 2000.

The 2007-2008 global financial crisis, often referred to as the Great Recession, was a complex and multifaceted event that shook the foundations of the global economy. The crisis was characterized by a sharp decline in stock markets, a freeze in credit markets, and a significant rise in unemployment. It was a confluence of several factors, both domestic and international, that led to this economic downturn, which had far-reaching consequences for individuals, businesses, and governments worldwide.

One of the primary causes of the crisis was the bursting of the U.S. housing bubble. For years, the housing market had been buoyed by lax lending standards and the proliferation of subprime mortgages. These loans were given to borrowers with poor credit histories or minimal income, often with low initial interest rates that were expected to adjust sharply higher in the future. When these adjustable-rate mortgages began to reset, many borrowers found themselves unable to afford the increased payments, leading to a surge in foreclosures.

The securitization of these subprime mortgages played a critical role in spreading the risk globally. Mortgage-backed securities (MBS) and collateralized debt obligations (CDOs) were created by bundling these loans together and selling them to investors. Ratings agencies, such as Moody's and Standard & Poor's, gave high ratings to many of these complex financial instruments, misleading investors about their true risk. When the housing market declined, the value of these securities plummeted, leading to massive losses for financial institutions worldwide.

Another significant factor was the prevalence of derivatives, particularly credit default swaps (CDS), which were essentially insurance against default. These swaps were traded over-the-counter, meaning they were not standardized and not necessarily reported to any regulatory body. As a result, the market for CDS became a shadow banking system, with trillions of dollars in notional value, that was largely unregulated and opaque. When the housing market began to fail, these swaps turned out to be worthless, causing further instability in the financial system.

Regulatory failures also contributed to the crisis. Financial institutions were allowed to grow too large and become "too big to fail," meaning that their collapse would have systemic consequences. The deregulation of the financial sector in the 1990s and 2000s, such as the repeal of the Glass-Steagall Act, which separated commercial and investment banking, allowed for riskier financial practices. Additionally, the failure of regulators to adequately supervise the growing shadow banking system and the issuance of subprime mortgages contributed to the buildup of systemic risks.

The impact of the crisis was exacerbated by the interconnectedness of the global financial system. As financial institutions in one country suffered losses, the effects were felt around the world. The decline in the U.S. housing market led to a domino effect, with banks in Europe and elsewhere that had invested in U.S. securities suffering significant losses. This interconnectedness meant that the crisis quickly became a global phenomenon.

The years following the crisis were marked by government interventions to stabilize the financial system. In the United States, the Troubled Asset Relief Program (TARP) was implemented to bail out major banks and other financial institutions. Central banks around the world lowered interest rates to near-zero levels and engaged in quantitative easing to inject liquidity into the markets. These measures helped to prevent a complete collapse of the financial system but did not prevent the subsequent recession.

The Great Recession had profound effects on the global economy, including a sharp increase in unemployment, a decline in consumer spending, and a significant reduction in economic growth. It also led to a wave of government stimulus programs to boost demand and encourage economic recovery.

In the aftermath of the crisis, there were significant changes in the regulatory environment to prevent future crises. The Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act was passed in the United States, introducing measures such as increased capital requirements for banks, the creation of the Financial Stability Oversight Council to monitor systemic risks, and the establishment of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau to protect consumers.

Despite these measures, the question remains whether similar events could happen again. While the specific causes of the 2007-2008 crisis may not repeat themselves exactly, there is always the potential for new financial crises. The financial industry is dynamic, and new products and practices can introduce unforeseen risks. The rise of digital currencies, for example, introduces new complexities and potential risks to the financial system.

Moreover, the issue of "too big to fail" banks remains, as these institutions continue to grow and dominate the financial landscape. If they were to fail, the systemic consequences could be similar to those seen in the last crisis. Additionally, the pace of technological change and the increasing interconnectedness of the global financial system mean that systemic risks can arise from unexpected sources.

To mitigate the risk of future crises, it is essential to maintain robust regulatory oversight, ensure that financial institutions are adequately capitalized, and that systemic risks are identified and managed. Continuous monitoring and analysis of the financial system, together with international cooperation, can help to create a more resilient global financial architecture. However, the nature of financial crises is that they often arise from unforeseen events or the buildup of risks that are not recognized until it is too late.

In conclusion, the 2007-2008 global financial crisis was a result of a combination of factors, including the bursting of the U.S. housing bubble, the securitization and sale of subprime mortgages, the proliferation of derivatives, regulatory failures, and the interconnectedness of the global financial system. While significant reforms have been implemented to prevent a recurrence, the potential for new crises remains. It is crucial for policymakers, regulators, and financial institutions to remain vigilant and adapt to the evolving financial landscape to minimize the risk of future economic turmoil.

The philosophy of free will and determinism has been a longstanding debate among philosophers for centuries. At its core, this debate revolves around whether human actions are determined by external factors such as genetics, environment, past experiences, and social conditioning, or if they result from freely chosen decisions made by individuals themselves. In other words, does our future unfold according to predetermined causes and effects, or do we possess the power to shape our own destiny? This question lies at the heart of what it means to be human, and answers vary widely depending on one's perspective and beliefs. 

On one hand, determinists argue that every event, including human actions, is caused by prior events and circumstances, which implies that everything we do is predetermined. According to this view, even thoughts and intentions that seem to arise spontaneously within us are ultimately traceable back to prior causes. Determinists often appeal to scientific advancements in fields such as neuroscience, psychology, and physics to support their position. For example, studies have shown that brain activity patterns can predict certain types of behavior before they occur, suggesting that our choices may not be entirely under our control. Furthermore, quantum mechanics suggests that even subatomic particles follow strict probabilistic laws that govern their behavior, raising questions about whether true indeterminacy exists anywhere in the universe.

However, opponents of determinism contend that humans retain some degree of autonomy over their lives. They assert that while environmental influences certainly play a significant role in shaping who we are and what we do, there remains room for individual freedom and choice. One common argument against determinism rests on the concept of moral responsibility. If all actions were predetermined, then why hold people accountable for things beyond their control? Moreover, if our choices lack significance, how could we ever truly praise or blame anyone for anything? Proponents of libertarian free will advance another challenge to determinism - the idea that consciousness itself cannot be reduced to purely physical processes; rather than being slaves to causality, we must acknowledge a non-physical aspect of ourselves that transcends material reality. 

Despite these objections, some versions of compatibilist theory attempt to reconcile free will with determinism. Compatibilists suggest that free will needn't require complete indeterminism but instead involve "self-forming" or self-organizing systems where multiple factors interact to produce novel outcomes without violating deterministic principles. In this sense, though our choices might still be influenced heavily by external forces, we nevertheless exercise agency when making them because the outcome isn't fixed from the beginning. 

Ultimately, resolving the conflict between free will and determinism seems impossible due to fundamental differences in perspectives and worldviews. Some adhere firmly to religious convictions emphasizing divine intervention or spiritual realms that influence human affairs; others rely solely on empirical evidence amassed through observation and experimentation. However, despite the divide, both sides share a deep desire to understand human nature and find meaning within an increasingly complex world. Perhaps more importantly, exploring these ideas allows us to better appreciate the nuances of existence and develop empathy towards those whose views differ significantly from our own. By engaging openmindedly with opposing viewpoints, we enrichen our understanding of what it means to exist as sentient beings navigating life together amidst countless variables influencing each step forward. Ultimately, embracing uncertainty and acknowledging mystery strengthens our capacity for compassionate coexistence regardless of which side of the debate we fall upon. Therefore, let us continue grappling collectively toward wisdom regarding free will versus determinism - maybe someday we will arrive at truth...or perhaps simply gain insight into the enduring beauty of inquiry itself! 

In conclusion, whether one believes in free will or determinism depends largely on personal conviction and faith. While science provides valuable insights into human behavior, it cannot definitively resolve the debate. Instead of striving for proof or disproof, perhaps we should aim for balance between accepting our place within natural order and cultivating our unique capacities as thinking, feeling beings capable of shaping our surroundings through intention, choice, and action.

In the vast, interconnected web of social structures that compose the modern world, education emerges as a cornerstone, intricately woven into the fabric of economic development. The link between education and economic growth is a subject that has long captivated scholars, policymakers, and educators alike. It is a relationship that is both intuitive and complex, with layers of causality and correlation that intertwine and reinforce one another in a dynamic dance of progress and enlightenment.

The foundation of this link is rooted in the concept of human capital. Human capital refers to the attributes of a population that, in turn, affect their productive capacity. These attributes include education, skills, health, and other factors that contribute to an individual's ability to produce goods and services. When education is improved within a society, the human capital is enhanced, leading to a workforce that is more skilled, adaptable, and capable of driving innovation and productivity.

Education equips individuals with the tools necessary to understand and manipulate their environment, leading to technological advancements and the efficient use of resources. As workers become more educated, they can perform tasks more efficiently and create new products and processes that propel economic growth. This is particularly evident in today’s knowledge-based economies, where information and technology play a critical role in productivity. The advent of the digital age has further cemented the importance of education in economic growth, as economies increasingly rely on high-skilled labor to drive innovation and compete on a global scale.

In addition to enhancing skills and knowledge, education also fosters entrepreneurial spirit. Educated individuals are more likely to spot business opportunities and possess the confidence and competence to seize them. Entrepreneurship is a vital engine of economic growth as it creates new companies, opens up new markets, and nurtures new industries. The ripple effects of successful entrepreneurial ventures are manifold; they create jobs, increase competitiveness, and stimulate further economic activity.

Moreover, education leads to a more equitable distribution of income and can be a powerful tool in breaking the cycle of poverty. By providing individuals with the skills to secure better-paying jobs, education can elevate the overall standard of living and expand the middle class. A more substantial middle class is crucial for a stable and growing economy because it ensures a broad base of consumers and a diversified demand for goods and services.

The relationship between education and economic growth is also reflected in the aggregate productivity of a nation. A more educated population can lead to collective problem-solving, resulting in more efficient businesses and institutions. This collective intelligence can drive public policy and create a conducive environment for economic activity. Education fosters not only technical skills but also soft skills, such as critical thinking, communication, and teamwork, which are increasingly important in the modern labor market.

Furthermore, the impact of education on economic growth can be observed through the lens of international development. Developing countries that have invested heavily in education have often seen dramatic growth rates. Countries in East Asia, such as South Korea and Singapore, serve as quintessential examples of how education can transform economies. These countries prioritized education after World War II, which laid the groundwork for their transition from low-income to high-income nations within a few decades.

However, it is crucial to recognize that the link between education and economic growth is not automatic. The quality and relevance of education are paramount. Educational systems that do not align with the needs of the economy can lead to underemployment and skills mismatches,

George Orwell's Animal Farm is a classic political allegory that has been interpreted in many different ways. One of the most common interpretations is that the novel is a critique of the Soviet Union under Joseph Stalin. In this interpretation, the pigs represent the Communist Party, the other animals represent the Russian people, and the farm itself represents the Soviet Union.

The pigs are initially seen as the leaders of the revolution, and they promise to create a society where all animals are equal. However, once they are in power, they quickly become corrupt and oppressive. They begin to exploit the other animals, and they eventually create a system of government that is just as bad as the one that existed before the revolution.

The other animals are initially fooled by the pigs' promises, but they eventually come to see the truth. They realize that the pigs are only interested in power, and they are not willing to share it with the other animals. The animals eventually rebel against the pigs, but they are defeated. The pigs then establish a totalitarian regime, and they rule the farm with an iron fist.

Animal Farm is a powerful allegory that shows how easily a revolution can be corrupted. The novel also shows how dangerous it is to give too much power to one group of people. The pigs in the novel are a cautionary tale about the dangers of totalitarianism.

In addition to being a critique of the Soviet Union, Animal Farm can also be interpreted as a critique of other political systems. The novel shows how any system of government can be corrupted, and it warns against the dangers of giving too much power to any one group of people.

Animal Farm is a timeless classic that is still relevant today. The novel is a reminder that the fight for freedom and equality is never over. It is also a reminder that we must always be vigilant against the dangers of totalitarianism.

The Facial Action Coding System (FACS) is a groundbreaking technology that has the potential to revolutionize the way we learn and interact in the classroom. This software, developed by Professor Thomas Huang of the Beckman Institute for Advanced Science, is capable of interpreting the subtlest of facial expressions to identify a range of emotions. The technology has already been tested in various educational settings and has shown promising results. In this essay, I will argue that the use of FACS to read the emotional expressions of students in a classroom is valuable and can have a positive impact on education.

One of the most significant benefits of FACS is that it allows teachers to tailor their approach to individual student needs. In a traditional classroom setting, it can be challenging for teachers to gauge the emotional state of their students, especially when students may be hesitant to express their feelings verbally. FACS solves this problem by providing a real-time emotional map of the classroom, empowering teachers to identify which students are confused, bored, or engaged. This information enables teachers to adjust their teaching methods and materials accordingly, ensuring that each student receives a personalized learning experience.

Another advantage of FACS is that it can help foster a sense of community and mutual understanding among students. Recognizing that facial expressions are universal, the system helps students see that they are not alone in their emotional responses. This shared understanding can foster collaboration and empathy, breaking down barriers of isolation and misunderstanding. In a world where social interactions are increasingly taking place online, FACS can help students develop essential social skills that are vital for success in the modern workplace.

Furthermore, FACS has the potential to improve student engagement and motivation. When students know that their emotions are being recognized and responded to, they are more likely to feel seen and heard. This can lead to increased participation, improved attendance, and better academic performance. Moreover, the software's ability to adapt lessons in real-time means that students can learn at their own pace, which can be particularly beneficial for students who may need extra support or for those who are advanced and need more challenge.

Despite the many benefits of FACS, some critics have raised concerns about the technology's efficacy in understanding complex human emotions and the nuances of face-to-face learning. However, as Dr. Huang points out, much of human communication is nonverbal. FACS is not intended to replace human interaction but to enhance it. The software is designed to recognize and respond to nonverbal cues, which can help teachers identify issues that may otherwise go unnoticed.

In conclusion, the use of FACS to read the emotional expressions of students in a classroom is valuable and has the potential to revolutionize education. By providing teachers with real-time information about their students' emotional states, fostering a sense of community and mutual understanding, improving student engagement and motivation, and enhancing human interaction, FACS can help create a more personalized, effective, and empathetic learning environment. As technology continues to evolve, it is essential that we embrace innovations like FACS that can help us better understand and connect with each other. The future of education, indeed, could well lie in the digital decoding of our smiles and frowns.

Vaccination has been one of the most transformative public health interventions in human history, saving countless lives and dramatically reducing the burden of infectious diseases. The concept of vaccination, however, is not a modern one. It has roots that stretch back centuries, with various forms of immunity-inducing practices being observed and employed across different cultures.

The earliest recorded use of vaccination can be traced to the 18th century, when variolation--the practice of deliberately exposing individuals to a mild form of smallpox virus to prevent severe infection--was prevalent in parts of Asia, Africa, and the Americas. This was a risky procedure, with a significant mortality rate, but it was often the best available defense against a disease that was a major killer at the time.

The true breakthrough in vaccination came with the work of Edward Jenner in the late 18th century. In 1796, Jenner observed that milkmaids who had contracted a mild disease called cowpox did not develop smallpox. He hypothesized that the cowpox infection had somehow protected them from smallpox. To test this theory, he inoculated a young boy with material from a cowpox lesion and later exposed him to smallpox. The boy did not develop the disease, confirming the protective effect of cowpox against smallpox. This discovery led to the development of the first vaccine, known as the smallpox vaccine.

Jenner's work was met with skepticism and controversy, but the evidence of its effectiveness gradually convinced the medical community and the public. The smallpox vaccine was adopted widely, and by the 20th century, it had become a cornerstone of global health efforts. The World Health Organization (WHO) launched an international campaign in 1967 to eradicate smallpox, and by 1979, the disease was declared eradicated, thanks in large part to the success of vaccination.

The success of the smallpox vaccine paved the way for the development of other vaccines. In the early 20th century, scientists and doctors began to understand the principles of immunology, which laid the groundwork for the creation of vaccines against a variety of diseases. The 1920s saw the development of the first diphtheria and pertussis vaccines, followed by the measles vaccine in the 1960s and the mumps and rubella vaccines in the 1970s.

The advent of modern techniques in molecular biology and biotechnology in the latter half of the 20th century revolutionized vaccine development. These advancements led to the creation of new types of vaccines, including subunit vaccines, recombinant vaccines, and conjugate vaccines, which offered improved safety, efficacy, and stability.

One of the most significant breakthroughs in recent years has been the development of the mRNA vaccine technology, which was first explored as a potential vaccination approach in the 1990s. This technology has been instrumental in the rapid development of vaccines against COVID-19, demonstrating the potential for vaccines to be created more quickly in response to emerging infectious diseases.

Despite the significant progress made in vaccine development, challenges remain. The production of vaccines is a complex and expensive process, and many parts of the world still lack access to life-saving vaccines due to economic, logistical, and political barriers. Efforts are ongoing to address these issues through global vaccination initiatives, research into more affordable vaccine manufacturing methods, and the development of thermostable vaccines that can be stored and transported more easily.

The history of vaccine development is a testament to the power of scientific discovery and the relentless pursuit of public health. It is a story of innovation, controversy, and ultimately, the triumph of evidence-based medicine in improving the health and well-being of people around the world. As we continue to face new infectious diseases and the threat of pandemics, vaccines remain one of our most powerful tools in the fight against illness and disease.

There are several theories to the Islamisation process in Southeast Asia. Another theory is trade. Many settled in Indonesia, Singapore, and Malaysia. This is evident in the Arab-Indonesian, Arab-Singaporean, and Arab-Malay populations who were at one time very prominent in each of their countries. The second theory is the role of missionaries or Sufis.[citation needed] The Sufi missionaries played a significant role in spreading the faith by introducing Islamic ideas to the region.
