“Poems Comparison: “”To His Coy Mistress”” and “”My Last Duchess””” Research Paper

Table of Contents
 1. Introduction
 2. Treatment of women
 3. Views of women
 4. Views of themselves
 5. Works Cited

Introduction

The poetic rendition of the female subject has historically been a patriarchal domain for famous poets like Robert Browning and Andrew Marvell to create their masterpieces. In these poems, objectification of the female body and attitude towards women is clearly shown under the garb of romantic poetry. In this essay, I will compare “To His Coy Mistress” by Andrew Marvell and “My Last Duchess” by Robert Browning to show how these two apparently different poems are similar in their treatment of the female subject. The poems hide the patriarchal desire to look at a woman who is behind the veils, hidden and unattainable. Though the poems are apparently dissimilar, the tone of the narrators, their description of the object of their obsession, and the treatment of the female body suggest a connection that previously was unobserved. The theses I present in the paper are that the resemblances and divergences between the two poems and finally argue that they are thematically similar.

Treatment of women

The voices of the narrators in both poems seem uncannily similar. Both are egotistical misogynists. A woman, the object of obsession for both the narrators, is the forbidden erotic object that the poets want to capture in their poems. In these dramatic monologues, the poets show the narrators as dominating and egotistical men who feel a woman’s wish is insignificant. Duke Ferrara shows the envoy his last, and, presumably, dead wife’s portrait that he keeps concealed from the common eye. A duke is a proud man who feels that his last duchess was too frivolous, easy to please, and bestowed her smiles too generously on strangers. The narrator has an inflated male ego that boasts of the nothingness of female existence. This is apparent when he says, “I gave commands; / Then all smiles stopped together” (Browning 45-46). The masculine pride of the duke reduces the duchess to a mere object (a painting). He boasts of his power to stop her from smiling with just one command. The narrator clearly indicates that the female demeanor is controlled and ruled by the man’s wishes.

He is the master of the female ‘other,’ and therefore, has physical and emotional power over her. A similar rejection of the female identity is observed in Marvell’s poem. Marvell’s narrator tries to seduce his mistress, initially with sweet words of love, and then with morbid and grotesque imagery to frighten her into submission. Here too, the narrator tries to gain sexual favor from his mistress, even when she is “coy” and reluctant to engage in physical relations. Apparently, the narrator seems to have accepted her negation, but that is a fallacy that the poet wants the readers to believe with the use of words like “lady” and “if you … refuse” (Marvell 2-9). However, the narrator, in the tradition of courtly love, should have accepted the woman’s denial. Instead, he pursues her with unabashed fervor. He solicits her love even when she refuses his advances: “And you should if you please, refuse / … My vegetable love should grow” (9-11). This actually shows that the narrator was unable to accept the lady’s denial and continued to pursue her. Like the narrator of “Last Duchess”, here too, the narrator believes his wishes gained precedence over the woman’s denial. Both of them believe that the female ‘other’ did not have any individual identity, but was an appendage to the male ‘self’, and therefore, a man’s possession.

Views of women

Women in the poems are depicted as frivolous and flirtatious. Browning’s narrator openly declares to the foreign envoy that his last wife “had a heart” that was “too soon made glad” or easily “impressed” (25-26). Duke Ferrara disapproved of her easy manner and sweet disposition. He believed his wife’s love and attention should be his exclusive property. When the duchess did not differentiate between the men on whom she bestowed her “speech” or “blush”, it infuriated the duke (33-34). The sense of egotistic possession was so strong in the duke that he could not tolerate the Duchess’s good-natured smiles towards other men.

Thus, the natural female beauty in her smiles, blushes, or sweet manners did not inspire love in the narrator. Instead, we find swelling anger to the mild and compassionate nature of the duchess. These character traits that the duke disliked in the duchess were the epitome of feminine nature and therefore a source of her identity. However, the duke vehemently rejects her character and suspects her fidelity (Gardner 166). Similarly, Marvell’s narrator in “Coy Mistress” feels that the “coyness” in his mistress is a show of her flirtatiousness. He strongly believes that she was enjoying his overt sexual advances even though she was rejecting them. Thus, both the narrators believe that women have an enticing nature. They are frivolous and ‘coy’, devoid of any moral uprightness.

Objectification of the female body is another aspect present in both the poems. These poetic creations have a voyeuristic appeal for the poet as well as the readers. Vivid physical description of the women depicts the male gaze on the female body. In “Last Duchess” the duke and the foreign envoy, both men, are looking at the life-like portrait of the duchess. The painting becomes the voyeuristic window where the male gaze appraises the female body. The line “Will ‘t please you sit and look at her” is an invitation by the duke to the envoy to appreciate the female form in the duchess’s painting (Browning 5). This invitation contradicts the duke’s possessive nature expressed in the poem. On the contrary, he takes pleasure in the show. The use of words like “depth of passion” of the duchess’s “earnest glance” and the “blush” on her “cheeks” was actually drawing the envoy’s attention to her physical appearance (9-15). The deliberate drawing of the reader’s attention to the duchess’s body shows the voyeuristic pleasure the narrator drew from this exhibition of the painting. Marvell’s narrator in “Coy Mistress” gives a vivid description of his mistress’s physical attributes:

Two hundred to adore each breast,

But thirty thousand to the rest;

An age at least to every part,

And the last age should show your heart. (13-18)

This description of the female body is devoid of any pretention of romantic involvement. Instead, it is just a pretense of passionate address that is rejected at the very beginning of the third stanza when he brings forth his real perception of his mistress whose beauty he believes are mere ashes (Cousins 398). His perception of his mistress becomes more apparent when he metaphorically compares her attempts to safeguard her chastity as a mere folly for her “long-preserved virginity” he says will “turn to dust” (27-30). Therefore, he believes that a woman’s beauty “shall no more be found” and will turn her old-fashioned honor to “dust” and “ashes” if she continually rejects a lover’s advances (25-30). The woman’s cadaver is also an object of lust to the narrator: “then worms shall try / That long-preserved virginity” (28-29). This shows that the narrator believes that a woman is desired only for her beauty and once she grows old, all her charms are lost. Both the narrators believe that women’s beauty is skin-deep. Their voyeuristic description actually shows their perception of feminine beauty and attraction. Both the narrators openly display the woman’s body for voyeuristic viewing through the words and expressions in the poem.

Views of themselves

The narrators of the poems are but a mirror into the poet’s attitude towards the gender. Marvell’s witty and erotic poem skillfully hides the true attitude of the poet behind the narrator. However, the poem depicts the poet’s disgust towards the female form (Cousins 399). The physical descriptions of feminine grace and virtue are an ironical representation of the rude description of the female body. Similarly, Browning, through his narrator, expresses his attitude towards women. His idea of feminine conduct is piquantly speckled with Victorian morality (Gardner 167). Both the poets show no respect for female identity and strongly reject its presence through their overt masculine overtures towards the female ‘other’. Imagining frivolity and flirtatiousness as the main traits of female character, the poets show that women are in their social status and should suffer male dominance. The presence of the male gaze in the poems is a deliberate sexist trope to intensify the narrator’s and through them the poet’s, misogynistic attitude towards women. In conclusion, both “Last Duchess” and “Coy Mistress” trivializes the female body as an object controlled by man, thus denying them an individual identity.

The pursuit of energy independence has been a pressing concern for nations worldwide, with the need for alternative and sustainable sources of energy becoming increasingly evident as fossil fuel reserves dwindle and the effects of climate change become more pronounced. Renewable energy, in the form of wind, solar, hydroelectric, geothermal, and biomass, has emerged as a viable solution to this problem. In this essay, we will examine the role of renewable energy in achieving energy independence, focusing on its advantages over fossil fuels, challenges to its adoption, and the steps that can be taken to accelerate its implementation.

Advantages of Renewable Energy over Fossil Fuels

Renewable energy resources have several advantages over traditional fossil fuels. Firstly, they are virtually inexhaustible due to their inherent ability to replenish themselves naturally, unlike fossil fuels, which are finite resources that will eventually run out. This ensures that renewable energy sources can provide a reliable and sustainable source of energy for generations to come. Secondly, renewable energy sources emit far less greenhouse gases and other pollutants than fossil fuels, reducing the harmful impact on the environment and mitigating the effects of climate change. Finally, renewable energy technologies are becoming increasingly efficient, cost-effective, and scalable, making them more competitive with fossil fuels economically.

Challenges to the Adoption of Renewable Energy

Despite these advantages, the adoption of renewable energy faces several challenges. One major obstacle is the initial capital investment required for the development and deployment of renewable energy infrastructure. This can be particularly daunting for developing countries with limited financial resources. Additionally, renewable energy sources are often subject to fluctuations in availability due to factors such as weather conditions or geographical constraints, necessitating the development of efficient storage technologies to ensure a reliable supply. Finally, there is resistance from fossil fuel industries and their lobbyists, who stand to lose significant profits if renewable energy sources become the primary source of energy.

Steps to Accelerate the Implementation of Renewable Energy

To overcome these challenges and accelerate the adoption of renewable energy, several steps can be taken by governments, industries, and citizens alike. Governments can play a crucial role by implementing policies and incentives that encourage the transition to renewable energy sources. This may include offering subsidies, tax breaks, and feed-in tariffs for renewable energy projects, as well as setting ambitious targets for the use of renewable energy in the electricity grid. Industries can contribute by investing in research and development of renewable energy technologies and adopting renewable energy solutions in their operations. Finally, individuals can make a difference by adopting renewable energy solutions in their homes and lifestyles, such as installing solar panels or using energy-efficient appliances.

Conclusion

In conclusion, achieving energy independence requires a shift away from fossil fuels towards renewable energy sources. Renewable energy offers numerous advantages over fossil fuels in terms of sustainability, environmental impact, and cost-effectiveness. However, challenges such as initial capital investment, fluctuations in availability, and resistance from vested interests must be overcome. Governments, industries, and citizens can all play a role in accelerating the implementation of renewable energy by adopting policies, investing in research, and adopting renewable energy solutions in their daily lives. By working together, we can create a future where renewable energy provides a reliable and sustainable source of energy for generations to come.

Brooks’ “A Song in the Front Yard” & Blake’s “The Sick Rose” Poems Essay

A picture of a child in “A Song in the Front Yard”

In the poem “A Song in the Front Yard” we get a picture of a child who needs and wants to explore the world beyond her front yard. She knows that there is a bigger world beyond her restricting boundary wall, “I’ve stayed in the front yard all my life,”(Line 1), and seeks to explore the world. Her sheltered childhood has forced her to think about what might be beyond these boundaries. “I want a peek at the back” (Line 2). This simple insight indicates that she feels simply exploring the backyard may be a good starting point. “To where the charity children play. I want a good time today. They do some wonderful things.

They have some wonderful fun”. (Lines 8-10) the child feels that since other children are having fun, she ought to be part of that larger experience. The poem is about restrictions placed on a person that chain his desire to explore and learn. Though these boundaries are created for our protection often they seem like chains.

The child in ‘A sick Rose’

The poem, A sick Rose, by William Blake on the other hand deals with the subject of a rose and worm. Now when we compare the two poems, they initially appear less common. But upon closer analysis, we notice many similarities. In both cases, a fragile subject is under study. In the first poem, it was the child who we all know is quite fragile. In this poem, it’s a rose which by nature is delicate. Both the child and the rose are suffering from an obsessive love of someone. In the first case, the child is suffering because of over-protection. The parents love the child and want him to stay within the front yard boundary of the house.

But the child is not happy with this restriction, it is eating on him. The other poem deals in a similar fashion with the delicate subject who is being eaten away by the obsessive love of a worm. The worm is attached to the rose because it loves the subject but that love is bad for the rose. In almost the same manner, the overprotection of parents is bad for the child.

The child is being told all sorts of things to justify overprotection: “My mother sneers, but I say it’s fine how they don’t have to go in at quarter to nine. My mother, she tells me that Johnnie Ma will grow up to be a bad woman.” (Lines 11-14) but the child doesn’t agree with her mom. She doesn’t probably even understand why people who stay out would grow up to be bad. In her small mind, the child is desperately thinking of the world beyond her house. She wants to be as carefree as the children in the street.

The child wants to be free, to be able to stay out longer, to experience the wonders of the world and we must all understand that it is extremely for a child to be able to explore. A child who is not given the chance to do so becomes dull in almost the same manner as the love of the worm withers away the rose.

Conclusion

Love in its obsessive form is always negative and never desirable. It is one thing to love someone and it is another to chain that person down thinking that this is love. In both poems, we learn about the obsessive kind of love. Parents’ love for the child is a positive force but when it is so restrictive that it inhibits the growth of a child, it becomes a negative force that must be countered. Children are very delicate and encouragement is to them like water is to flowers. They need their parent’s love and support to see and explore the world and they want parents to encourage this exploration. However, when it doesn’t happen, the child can suffer much in the same way as the rose suffers.

Ben was scratching the bottom of his pudding cup when he heard the ping. It technically wasn't his pudding, but it'd been in the staff refrigerator for 2 weeks staring at him. There were two, and neither had been touched. They were bound to go bad soon anyway, at least that's what he told himself. It was worth the wait, he wondered why he didn't buy it more. Grad school was the answer to that. If it wasn't less than 20 cents a serving it wasn't on his grocery list. With student loans kicking in as soon as he graduated in 3 months that probably wasn't going to change much. Sometimes he chastised himself for his choices. If he'd just pursued Engineering or Finance he'd probably be making 6 figures. Sometimes he blamed his parents for telling him to pursue what he loved. Astronomy to him, was a noble cause, the final frontier. Our species very destiny lay above. What he was doing actually mattered. Better than screwing over home owners or helping a natural gas company destroy more of the earth. The night shift at his state university's lab didn't exactly help his ego though. The ping wouldn't either. He was there purely to monitor equipment and alert anyone of any malfunctions. That's what the ping seemed to be. The satellite had picked up a near earth object. Relatively regular occurrence, it was usually another satellite though. This was too far out to be another one satellite. Ben was in the middle of logging it when he got another ping. It was closer now. He decided to check if Dr. Schlitt was still around editing her latest paper. In a year of doing this, it was already the most interesting thing that had happened for him, and this might get him on her good side. As he picked up the phone he realized it was the first time he'd used a chorded phone in at least 3 years. It took two rings for her to answer. "Hello?" "Dr. Schlitt?" "Speaking." "I've got a couple pings, want to check them out?" "Just a second." Ben quickly quit out of the facebook tab, and opened up his journal to pretend like he was taking notes. "I was saving those for the end of my cleanse." "What?" She pointed at the empty pudding cup tipped over from the metal spoon. Ben's cheeks burned. "Oh s-." She waved her hand. "It's fine, what are we looking at?" He rolled back in his chair as she took control of the station. "That's," she trailed off. Another Ping. "No." "Did I do something wrong?" Ben asked. Her phone rang. She picked it up immediately. "Gil." Ben could hear the murmur of her phone, her eyes beginning to bulge. "Is everything ok?" He heard a hissing, then saw the puddle forming at her shoes. "Are you ok?" She wailed. He stood, taking her by her shoulders. "I'm calling an ambulance." She finally met his eyes. "Call your parents, tell them you love them." "Ooooh," he said like he'd just been given the answer to a trivia question. "There is nothing more terrifying in this world than the knowledge you can do nothing." She fled the room. His eyes fell to the puddle on the floor. "Gross." He walked to the kitchen and grabbed the last cup of pudding.

Driverless Cars: A Promising Future or an Intrusive Technology? 

The emergence of driverless cars is an exciting development in the automobile industry as we look to the future. However, there are several challenges and drawbacks to consider before accepting this technology as the way of the future in our everyday lives. In this essay, I will argue against the development of driverless cars.

To start, the technological constraints of autonomous vehicles raise several doubts. Although driverless cars have improved their capabilities, there is still a lot of work to be done regarding their practicality. These vehicles are still not capable of handling high-speed driving, and drivers need vigilance, making them more like semi-driverless vehicles, which defeats the purpose of the technology. It would be more practical to focus on improving traditional vehicles instead of developing a futuristic, impractical technology. 

Moreover, the privacy concern associated with the cameras installed to monitor drivers is a serious drawback of this technology. Although the goal of ensuring driver engagement is crucial when using driverless cars, it's an invasion of drivers privacy to install surveillance systems that monitor and evaluate every move made in the car. The thought of being watched by the manufacturer constantly raises a valid privacy concern, and the stress it creates could cause distracted driving, leading to more accidents than before driverless car technology.

In conclusion, driverless car technology seems unnecessary and intrusive to the lives of people, given the current limitations and challenges of the technology. The costs of the required smart roads for the vehicles' compatibility with existing infrastructure are daunting, with no clear idea of who should bear the expenses of the required changes. Therefore, we need to focus on developing practical solutions for our existing vehicles instead of investing resources in a technology that has yet to prove its worth. It's essential that we consider practical, economic, and personal concerns before making significant technological advancements in the future of transportation.

As a scientist at NASA, I have had the opportunity to study the Face on Mars, a mesa located in the Cydonia region of the red planet. Recently, I had a conversation with someone who believes that the Face was created by aliens. While I understand the fascination with the idea of extraterrestrial life, I must respectfully disagree with this belief. The Face on Mars is not a creation of aliens, but a natural landform that can be explained by geological processes.
One of the main claims supporting the idea that the Face is a natural landform is its similarity to other mesas on Earth. The article "Unmasking the Face on Mars" mentions that the Face is similar to Earth's buttes or mesas. This means that the geological processes that formed the Face are similar to those that form mesas on our own planet. It is not surprising that Mars, a planet with similar geological processes, would have similar landforms.

Another piece of evidence from the article that supports the natural origin of the Face is the laser altimetry data. This data confirmed that the Face is a natural landform, similar to other mesas in the Cydonia region. The data showed that the Face has the same elevation and slope as the surrounding terrain, indicating that it is not a structure created by intelligent life.

Furthermore, the article explains that the Face is located at a potential ancient Martian ocean boundary. This location raises questions about Mars' past and its geological history, but it does not suggest the presence of alien life. The fact that the Face is located in an area that was once possibly submerged underwater suggests that it was formed by geological processes that occurred over millions of years, such as erosion and deposition.

Finally, it is important to note that the images of the Face taken by NASA's Mars Global Surveyor in 1997 dispelled the conspiracy theories about the Face being an artificial structure. The images showed that the Face is a natural landform, with features that can be explained by geological processes.
While the idea of alien life on Mars is an exciting one, it is important to rely on scientific evidence when forming conclusions about the nature of celestial bodies. The evidence from the article "Unmasking the Face on Mars" supports the claim that the Face is a natural landform, similar to those found on Earth. The similarities between the Face and other mesas, the laser altimetry data, and the location of the Face at a potential ancient Martian ocean boundary all suggest that it is a natural landform. I hope this argument has convinced you that the Face on Mars is not a creation of aliens, but a fascinating geological feature that continues to capture our imagination.

In the realm of literature, the aftermath of colonialism left an indelible imprint, giving rise to a distinctive genre known as post-colonial literature. This literary movement emerged as a powerful voice, echoing the experiences, struggles, and triumphs of nations grappling with the aftermath of colonial rule. At the heart of post-colonial literature lies the intricate interplay of culture and language, a dynamic that shapes the narratives and perspectives presented within these works.

In the fictional nation of Eldoria, the echoes of colonialism still reverberated, casting a long shadow over its cultural landscape. The scars of a colonial past were etched into the very fabric of society, influencing language, customs, and identities. Eldoria's rich cultural heritage had been interwoven with the language of its former colonizers, creating a linguistic tapestry that bore the marks of both assimilation and resistance.

Amidst this cultural crossroads, a young woman named Anya emerged as a symbol of the nation's struggle for self-expression and cultural reclamation. Anya's journey mirrored that of Eldoria itself, as she navigated the complexities of her identity, caught between the remnants of colonialism and the yearning for cultural authenticity.

Anya's passion for literature drew her to the works of post-colonial writers, authors who dared to challenge the dominant narratives imposed by colonial powers. Through their words, she discovered a voice that resonated with her own experiences, a voice that articulated the struggles and aspirations of her people.

Inspired by these literary pioneers, Anya embarked on her own literary journey, determined to contribute to the growing body of post-colonial literature. Her writing became a powerful tool of resistance, a means to reclaim her cultural heritage and assert Eldoria's unique identity.

Anya's words painted vivid portraits of Eldoria's vibrant culture, capturing the essence of its traditions, beliefs, and customs. She breathed life into the stories of her ancestors, weaving their tales into a tapestry of resilience and hope. Her characters embodied the struggles of a nation grappling with its colonial past, their voices echoing the collective yearning for liberation.

As Anya's literary prowess flourished, her works gained recognition beyond the borders of Eldoria. Her writing resonated with readers across the globe, transcending cultural and geographical boundaries. Through her words, she ignited a dialogue about the enduring legacies of colonialism and the power of literature as a force for change.

Anya's journey became a testament to the transformative power of post-colonial literature, its ability to bridge cultures, challenge oppressive narratives, and empower marginalized voices. Her story exemplified the resilience of the human spirit, its unwavering determination to rise above the shackles of the past and forge a path towards cultural self-determination.

And so, in the literary realm of post-colonialism, Anya's voice joined the chorus of countless others, each contributing to a symphony of resistance, resilience, and cultural reclamation. Their words echoed through time, carrying the hopes and dreams of nations emerging from the shadows of colonialism, illuminating a path towards a future where cultures thrived in harmony and voices united in a shared pursuit of liberation.

Curfews have been a contentious issue in society, particularly when it comes to their implementation regarding teenagers. Advocates for curfews argue that they serve as an effective means of keeping young people out of trouble and ensuring their safety. On the other hand, critics contend that curfews unfairly infringe on teenagers' rights and freedom, potentially causing more harm than good. This essay will explore both perspectives, examining the effectiveness of curfews in promoting safety and deterring negative behaviors among teenagers.

One of the primary arguments in favor of curfews is their potential to reduce crime and gang-related activities. Research has shown that implementing curfews can lead to a decrease in certain types of crime, particularly those associated with young people. For example, a study conducted in Los Angeles found that juvenile crime rates decreased by 29% during the first year after the implementation of a citywide curfew. Similarly, a study in Florida found that curfew enforcement led to a significant decrease in violent crime among teenagers.

Another argument for curfews is their ability to promote safety among teenagers. By requiring young people to be home at specific times, curfews can help protect them from dangerous situations. This is particularly important during late-night hours when the risk of being involved in accidents, encountering criminals, or engaging in risky behaviors is higher. Furthermore, curfews can encourage responsible decision-making among teenagers by fostering a sense of accountability and consequences for violating the established rules.

Curfews can also provide an opportunity for teenagers to develop important life skills, such as time management and organization. By adhering to a set schedule, young people can learn how to prioritize their time and activities, ensuring that they complete their homework, participate in extracurricular activities, and engage in leisure time without exceeding the imposed curfew. Additionally, maintaining a consistent sleep schedule can contribute to better overall health and academic performance, further supporting the potential benefits of curfews.

However, opponents of curfews argue that they infringe on teenagers' rights and freedom, leading to negative consequences. Critics point out that curfews can limit young people's ability to participate in after-school activities, such as sports, clubs, and volunteer work, which may have a positive impact on their personal and social development. Furthermore, some argue that curfews disproportionately affect low-income families and minority groups, creating barriers to equal opportunities and social mobility.

Additionally, opponents of curfews suggest that they may not be as effective as proponents claim. Research on the long-term effectiveness of curfews has produced mixed results, with some studies finding that the initial decrease in crime rates is not sustained over time. Furthermore, critics argue that curfews may simply shift criminal activities to earlier hours or drive them underground, making it more difficult for law enforcement to address the root causes of the problem.

In conclusion, the debate surrounding the effectiveness of curfews in keeping teenagers out of trouble and the potential interference with young people's lives is a complex issue with valid arguments on both sides. While proponents of curfews emphasize the potential benefits in reducing crime, promoting safety, and fostering responsible decision-making, opponents highlight the potential negative consequences on teenagers' rights and freedom, as well as the mixed evidence on their long-term effectiveness. Ultimately, it is essential to consider the specific context and needs of each community when determining the appropriateness and effectiveness of implementing curfews for teenagers.

The pristine rivers, lakes, and streams that once flowed through the heart of indigenous territories have now become the victims of an insidious and devastating phenomenon: water pollution. This pollution has far-reaching implications, not only for the environment but also for the rights and livelihoods of indigenous peoples. The indigenous peoples, who have lived in harmony with nature for millennia, are now witnessing the slow decay of their ancestral lands due to this unchecked exploitation of natural resources. In this essay, we will delve into the impact of water pollution on indigenous peoples' rights to land and explore the various ways in which this pollution is exacerbating existing inequalities and threatening the very survival of these communities.

Water is a fundamental aspect of indigenous cultures and lifestyles. It is not only a source of sustenance, but also a symbol of life, fertility, and the sacred connection between humans and the environment. Indigenous peoples have long held a deep respect for the water and the life it sustains, and their spiritual practices often revolve around the protection and preservation of this vital resource. As such, the pollution of water sources represents not only a physical threat to their well-being but also an assault on their cultural identity and spiritual beliefs.

The primary source of water pollution affecting indigenous lands is industrial activities, such as mining, oil extraction, and waste disposal. These industries often set up operations in indigenous territories due to the perceived lack of regulation and oversight, as well as the potential for economic gain. The consequences of this exploitation are manifold, including the contamination of water sources, loss of biodiversity, and the degradation of the land itself. The pollution of water sources not only makes it difficult for indigenous peoples to access clean water for drinking, cooking, and bathing, but also disrupts the delicate ecosystems that support their traditional ways of life.

The impact of water pollution on indigenous peoples' rights to land is multifaceted and complex. On one hand, the pollution of water sources has led to the displacement of indigenous communities, as they are forced to abandon their ancestral lands in search of clean water and arable land. This displacement not only disrupts their cultural and spiritual practices but also undermines their right to self-determination and autonomy. On the other hand, the pollution of water sources also serves to legitimize the encroachment of non-indigenous interests onto indigenous lands, as governments and corporations often cite the need for water resources to justify their exploitation of these territories.

Furthermore, the pollution of water sources has far-reaching implications for the health and well-being of indigenous peoples. The consumption of contaminated water can lead to a range of illnesses, including gastrointestinal diseases, skin irritations, and even more severe health issues such as cancer. This not only exacerbates existing health disparities between indigenous and non-indigenous populations but also places an additional burden on indigenous communities, who often lack access to adequate healthcare facilities and resources.

In order to address the issue of water pollution and its impact on indigenous peoples' rights to land, it is essential that governments and corporations take meaningful steps to protect and preserve these vital resources. This could include implementing stricter regulations on industrial activities, investing in the development of sustainable water management practices, and engaging in dialogue with indigenous communities to better understand their needs and concerns. Moreover, it is crucial that indigenous peoples are recognized as active stakeholders in the decision-making process, as their unique knowledge and perspective can contribute valuable insights into the conservation and management of water resources.

In conclusion, the pollution of water sources represents a significant threat to indigenous peoples' rights to land, as it not only jeopardizes their physical well-being and cultural identity but also undermines their right to self-determination and autonomy. It is incumbent upon governments, corporations, and society at large to take responsibility for the consequences of their actions and work to rectify the injustices faced by indigenous peoples. By recognizing and respecting the rights of indigenous peoples to their lands and resources, we can help to ensure a more equitable and sustainable future for all.

Hi, I'm a 6th grader and I'm gonna write an essay about why we should or shouldn't eat less meat.

Some people say we should eat less meat because it's better for the Earth. They say that it takes a lot of water and land to raise animals for food, and that it makes greenhouse gases that make the planet hotter. They also say that it's better for our health because meat has a lot of fat and salt, which can make us sick.

But I don't think we should stop eating meat altogether. Meat is a good source of protein, which is important for our bodies. It's also really tasty, and a lot of people enjoy eating it. Instead, I think we should just eat less meat and make sure we're eating it in a way that's good for the Earth.

One way we can do this is by eating more plant-based meals. Plants are a great source of protein too, and they don't make as many greenhouse gases as meat. We can also choose meat that's raised in a way that's better for the environment, like grass-fed beef.

Another reason we should eat less meat is because of animal welfare. Some animals are treated really badly on farms, and they don't have good living conditions. If we eat less meat, then there will be less demand for it and farms will have to treat their animals better.

But, I also think it's important to remember that not everyone can afford to eat meat, and that's okay. We should make sure that everyone has access to healthy food, whether it's meat or not.

In conclusion, I think we should eat less meat, but not completely stop eating it. We should make sure we're eating it in a way that's good for the Earth and for our health, and we should also think about animal welfare. By making these changes, we can have a healthier planet and healthier bodies.

Theodore Dreiser's novel "Sister Carrie" is a powerful exploration of social mobility in the late 19th century America. The protagonist, Carrie Meeber, embarks on a journey to escape her impoverished background and find a better life in the big city. The story follows her as she navigates through various social classes and experiences the harsh realities of American society.

Carrie's journey begins when she leaves her small town in Wisconsin to join her sister in Chicago. She is initially excited about the prospect of finding fame and fortune in the big city. However, upon arriving, she realizes that the path to success is not easy. She soon discovers that hard work and determination alone are not enough to lift her out of poverty. She struggles to make ends meet, working long hours in a factory and living in squalid conditions.

Carrie's fortunes begin to change when she meets and falls in love with Charles Drouet, a successful businessman. He offers her a chance to escape her miserable life and start anew. He provides her with money, clothes, and a luxurious lifestyle. However, their relationship is built on shaky grounds. Charles is more interested in using Carrie as a trophy to elevate his social status than in truly loving her.

Carrie's social mobility continues when she marries George Hurstwood, a wealthy man from a respected family. She moves into a grand mansion and becomes a member of high society. However, her marriage is not a happy one. George is deeply troubled and suffers from depression. He feels trapped in his marriage and unable to pursue his true passions.

Despite her social status, Carrie remains unhappy in her marriage. She longs for the excitement and freedom she once had as a struggling actress. She embarks on an affair with Robert Ames, a writer and philosopher. Their relationship is passionate and intellectually stimulating, but it also threatens to destroy her marriage and her social standing.

In the end, Carrie's journey towards social mobility is marked by both triumph and tragedy. She experiences the highs of wealth and fame, but also the lows of loneliness and despair. Her story serves as a powerful commentary on the harsh realities of American society, where social mobility is often achieved at great personal cost.

In conclusion, "Sister Carrie" is a compelling novel that explores the theme of social mobility through the life of its protagonist, Carrie Meeber. The story highlights the challenges and difficulties faced by those who aspire to rise above their humble beginnings, and the often-cruel nature of American society's obsession with status and wealth. Through Carrie's experiences, Dreiser offers a thought-provoking examination of the human condition and the pursuit of happiness in the face of adversity.

Individual Behavior and Communication Research Paper

Table of Contents
 1. Abstract
 2. Different Styles of Behavior
 3. Behavioral Styles and Elements of Communication
 4. Conclusion
 5. References

Abstract

Human Behavior is rather complex and dynamic. Psychologists and behaviorists have, over the years, research different aspects of behavior and attitudinal patterns. Some concluded similar findings while the others discovered unknown mesmerizing traits. Nonetheless, an individual rarely displays one style of behavior at all times. Therefore, it is not easy to associate a definite behavioral style with an individual. One behavioral approach may be predominant in his attitude. However, the style varies according to time and circumstances. Behavior is influenced by many external and internal factors.

As part of a team, an individual’s behavior is affected by the role he assumes and the responsibility he shoulders as well as the attitudes of his colleagues. He adopts a behavioral style and retains it as long as the team works together. Consequently, his written, verbal and non-verbal communication gets adapted to his behavioral approach. The messages he receives are interpreted by him accordingly and the messages he sends are construed by the recipient according to his style of behavior.

Different Styles of Behavior

A dominant or a pioneer-style is usually assumed by those team members who behave more as leaders and take initiative in proposing or pursuing an idea. An impressor tries to be in the supervisor’s good books and is more like a sycophant. An adventurer is a risk-taker and a speculator. He looks primarily at the advantages of undertaking a project or a business venture and makes contingency plans for overcoming anticipated disasters. A go-getter is an enthusiast and has an out-going personality. He is more likely to be successful than his colleagues. A director is sterner and very demanding of his teammates.

Behavioral Styles and Elements of Communication

The study of human behavior is rather challenging because behavior is complexly dynamic. The styles of attitudes and approaches towards behavior are influenced by several factors such as the environment, society, culture, religious affiliations, education, and family traditions and background. As circumstances vary, an individual assumes a behavioral style accordingly. It is likely that an individual takes on two or more behavioral styles at the same time or takes up a hybrid style which is a combination of two or more styles.

The versatility in behavioral styles is growing with the fast-moving world. Individuals assume various roles, interact with people from different backgrounds and cultures and are required to work as members of cross-functional teams in organizations. Today, as increasing emphasis is placed on employee empowerment and “organizational effectiveness”, the concept of working in teams is on the rise. As the “more we try to work as a team, the more important it becomes to recognize that people exhibit different behavioral styles” (Chaneski, 2006).

The individuals possessing different styles of behavior portray certain characteristics associated with their particular styles. However, it is unlikely that “that all people of a particular behavioral style exhibit all of the characteristics portrayed” (Chaneski, 2006). These characteristics as well as the elements of communication mutually impact each other. According to Wenger (1984), “Communication has seven elements: source, message, receiver, channel, effect, feeback and evaluation” (p. 1215). The source is the sender; the channel is the medium through which communication is carried out; effect includes the reaction of the recipient; feedback is the response from the recipient when he assumes the role of the sender; evaluation is the analysis concerning whether the message was received effectively (Wenger 1984).

Each individual would deliver a message in his style. Whether the message is received precisely is determined by the behavioral attitude of the intended audience and the medium used. Therefore, members of a team are ethically bound to use the right medium, appropriate words, and a softer tone when communicating with colleagues particularly in the case of foreign teammates and non-verbal communication. Cultural diversity within organizations is enhancing with overseas employment. “A Greek may see a contract as a formal statement announcing the intention to build a business… An Arab may be insulted by merely mentioning a contract” (Guffey 2006). Besides, a person possessing a director’s behavioral style may use a slightly harsh tone when writing a letter. As his real attitude can only be judged by non-verbal cues, a first-time recipient of his message may draw a negative connotation from it.

Conclusion

As personalities differ, so do behavioral styles. Some managers may be more demanding and stern while others would be more helpful and behave like leaders and role models. These varying attitudes have an impact on and at the same time, are affected by communication with colleagues. Differences in cultural and social diversity and the chances of wrong interpretation must be kept in mind when delivering a message.

References

Chaneskiki , Wayne i (2006). Find Articles – Understanding the Four Major Behavioral Styles .

Guffey, Mary Ellen (2006). Business Communication: Process and Product, 5 th Edition . Mason: Thomson South-Western.

Wenger, Karl (1984). Forestry Handbook, 2 nd Edition . New York: Wiley-IEEE.

Once upon a time, in the vast and intricate realm of nature, there existed a group of organisms often overlooked and underappreciated: fungi. These tiny beings, ranging from microscopic spores to enormous mushrooms, played a pivotal role in maintaining the balance and health of countless ecosystems across the planet. Their unique abilities and adaptations allowed them to thrive in even the most extreme environments, from the scorching deserts to the frigid arctic tundras.

Fungi are members of the kingdom Fungi, which is distinct from both plants and animals. Their bodies, called mycelia, are composed of threadlike filaments called hyphae that spread through soil, wood, and other organic matter. Fungi obtain nutrients by breaking down complex organic compounds into simpler ones, a process known as decomposition. They play a crucial role in the carbon cycle by releasing carbon dioxide back into the atmosphere during decomposition, while also storing carbon in the form of organic matter in the soil.

One of the most interesting aspects of fungi is their role in symbiotic relationships, which are essential to the functioning of many ecosystems. For example, mycorrhizal fungi form a symbiotic association with the roots of plants, where they extend their hyphae into the soil in search of water and nutrients. The fungi provide the plants with these essential resources, while the plants supply the fungi with carbohydrates generated through photosynthesis. This mutually beneficial relationship allows both organisms to thrive and supports the overall health of the ecosystem.

Fungi also play a critical role in bioremediation, which is the use of living organisms to clean up polluted environments. When soil or water is contaminated with harmful chemicals or heavy metals, fungi can help break down these toxins and render them harmless. This process is known as biodegradation, and it involves the production of enzymes and other specialized molecules by fungi that enable them to degrade a wide variety of pollutants.

One particularly impressive example of fungi's bioremediative abilities can be seen in the Chernobyl nuclear disaster site. After the 1986 explosion at the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant, large areas of land were contaminated with radioactive cesium-137. However, researchers were surprised to discover that the amount of cesium-137 in the soil began to decrease over time. Further investigation revealed that a species of fungus called Cladosporium sphaerospermum had evolved the ability to accumulate and sequester cesium-137 within its cells, effectively removing it from the environment.

Another fascinating application of fungi in bioremediation is their use in bioremediation of oil spills. When an oil spill occurs, oil-degrading bacteria are often introduced to the affected area to break down the pollutant. However, these bacteria can only colonize the surface of the oil, leaving a significant portion of the spill untouched. Enter the oleophilic fungi, which have a natural affinity for oil. These fungi can penetrate deeply into the oil-contaminated soil or water, effectively increasing the surface area available for degradation and accelerating the cleanup process.

In conclusion, fungi play a vital role in the functioning of ecosystems and are essential for maintaining the balance of nature. Their unique abilities and adaptations make them invaluable in bioremediation efforts, as they help clean up polluted environments and restore ecosystem health. Without their tireless efforts, the planet would be a far less hospitable place for all living organisms, including ourselves. So next time you're out for a hike or simply admiring the beauty of nature, take a moment to appreciate the unsung heroes of the fungi kingdom that make it all possible.

Sandstone serpents wound their red bodies up and down the columns of the temple. Julbert followed Antoine into the dark mouth of the temple, tasting the dust and the stale, ancient air. Water dripped through cracks in the sandstone walls, draining into rectangular pools that were stained green with age and light-loathing algae. Julbert's lights bounced wildly off the walls, revealing painted figures of old men and women, stooped over their canes or lying on their beds with their eyes closed and mouths hanging open. A great stone blocked their passage to the throat of the temple. The stone was as tall as a man, and carved into a smooth disc. "Shall we break it, or move it?" Antoine asked, resting his hand against the cool sandstone wall. "How much do you think it ways?" "Oh, I'd say at least one ton. Perhaps two." "Let's just move it, then." Julbert positioned himself on the right side of the disc, crouching so Antoine could fit above him. Together, the two amateur delvers grunted and pushed against the disc. Stone ground against stone, and the disc wheeled to the side to reveal another deep, dark passage. "Well done," Antoine said, slapping Julbert on the shoulder, "With any luck "AT LAST, " a voice boomed out from the darkness. "Did you say something?" Julbert asked. "No." Antoine and Julbert peered down the dark passage. They looked at each other. They looked back to the passage. "YOU HAVE COME TO WORSHIP. " Antoine cupped a hand to his mouth, and projected his voice down the passage, "Yes, excuse me. Worship what?" "ME, OF COURSE. " "And who, exactly, are you?" Jets of fire shot out from the darkness, and a hundred torches burst into flames with a series fwoompfs. Julbert and Antoine watched as the fires illuminated the chamber, littered with fine jewels and gold and the threadbare remains of expensive clothes. In the center of the chamber, a bald man sat on a dais, raised several feet off the ground. The man opened his black-painted eyelids as slowly as the rising sun. "I AM YOUR GOD. " His scalp was laced with intricate tattoos, formed into the shape of a crown. "YOU MAY APPROACH, AND WORSHIP AT MY FEET. " "Why does he want us to to worship his feet?" "I don't know. He looks like he's been here a while, perhaps he's confused." "Oh, my grandfather was confused, too. He had Alzheimers." "They didn't cure him?" "Of course! He's alright n "I AM NOT CONFUSED. I AM YOUR GOD AND YOU ARE IN AWE OF ME. " Antoine and Julbert looked back at the raised dais, their faces alight with curiosity. "Excuse me," Antoine lifted a finger, "Might I ask, how long have you been down here?" The bald God permitted a smile to cross his face. He nodded at Antoine, "AT LAST. YOU RECOGNIZE MY GREAT POWER. YOU HAVE HEARD MY LEGEND, AND COME TO WORSHIP "Legend?" Julbert echoed. "YOU MEAN YOU DO NOT KNOW? " Julbert shuffled his feet. Antoine put a hand to his mouth, and coughed. "BUT MY LEGEND- IT WAS PASSED DOWN, FROM GENERATION TO GENERATION. " The bald God put his hands on his knees, and leaned forward over his crossed-legs. Julbert and Antoine looked at each other. "I SEALED MYSELF IN THIS TOMB, FIVE HUNDRED YEARS PAST. NOW, I RETURN TO RULE YOUR MORTAL WORLD. " "To rule?" "YES. " Julbert turned to Antoine, and spoke with a low voice, "Are the translators broken? My ear piece seems fine, but you can never tell with these things." "No, I think they're working," Antoine whispered back, "I think he's just confused." "FOOLS! I AM NOT CONFUSED. I AM YOUR GOD! YOU QUAKE BEFORE MY IMMORTALITY. " "Ohhh!" Julbert gave Antoine a knowing nod. "Ah, of course," Antoine nodded back. "Excuse me, sir, how long did you say you were in this tomb?" "FIVE HUNDRED YEARS. WHILE YOUR PATHETIC MORTAL CIVILIZATIONS HAVE RISEN AND FALLEN, I HAVE MERELY SLUMBERED." "Well, as it happens, I am two hundred and seven. And Julbert over here, he just celebrated his two hundred and fiftieth." "It was really quite a party. We went deep sea diving," Julbert closed his eyes, and smiled. "Yes, it was," Antoine patted Julbert's shoulder. "Next year, we're going to Venus." "TWO..... HUNDRED..... WAIT. ARE YOU IMMORTAL? " "Yes, of course." "And..... and you, too? " The strength was waned from the bald God's voice. "Afraid so." "So..... is EVERYONE immortal? " Julbert and Antoine's heads bobbed simultaneously. "AH. " The bald God let out a rushing sigh, billowing up clouds of dust in the torchlight. "WELL, COULD YOU HELP ME STAND UP? I'VE BEEN SITTING FOR A VERY LONG TIME. "

With the shortage of physicians and surgeons and increase in demand worldwide due to situations such as the COVID-19 pandemic, there is a growing interest in finding solutions to help address the shortage. One solution is to train more physicians and surgeons to meet the growing demand. To support more students enroll and graduate, universities are increasing the number of medical schools and residency programs. Another solution is to optimize the workflow of surgeons and physicians. This can be done through standardization of workflow or automation of specific workflows. In this study, we propose a methodology to optimize the workflow of a urologist and his staff. The methodology is based on a new ontology for urology, the Urology Domain Ontology (UROD), to represent workflows. The UROD is a domain ontology for urology developed based on the basic concepts of the Common Logic ontology. A workflow is represented by a UROD ontology class and the steps in the workflow are represented by UROD instances. The UROD ontology is implemented in Protege. Keywords: ontology, workflow, urology Referencing: "The Urology Domain Ontology (UROD): An Ontology for Representing Urology-Specific Workflows," A. G. Bennett, G. Zhang, G. T. Campbell, R. T. Snodgrass, I. Siddiqui, BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making, 19 (1), 102 (2019)

A city council is considering the implementation of a 10 pm weekday curfew and a midnight weekend curfew for teenagers. While some may argue that this is an infringement on individual freedom, I strongly believe that curfews are necessary to keep teenagers safe and out of trouble.

Firstly, curfews provide a sense of structure and boundaries for teenagers. By setting a specific time for them to be home, it reduces the risk of them being out late and potentially getting into dangerous situations. For example, if they are out on the streets after dark, they may be more likely to encounter drugs, gangs, and other negative influences.

Secondly, curfews allow teenagers to spend more quality time with their families. In today's fast-paced world, it can be easy for teenagers to become disconnected from their parents. By having a set time for them to be home, parents can spend time with their children, have conversations about their lives, and help them navigate the challenges they face.

Finally, curfews promote a sense of responsibility and respect for the law. By enforcing a curfew, teenagers are taught that there are consequences for breaking rules and that it is important to follow the law. This can help to instill a sense of respect for authority and a commitment to doing the right thing.

In conclusion, while some may argue that curfews are an infringement on individual freedom, I strongly believe that they are necessary to keep teenagers safe and out of trouble. By providing a sense of structure, allowing for more quality time with families, and promoting a sense of responsibility and respect for the law, curfews can have a positive impact on the lives of teenagers and their families.

As the sun rose over the sprawling city, the sound of sneakers squeaking against the polished gym floor filled the air. The basketball court was alive with the energy of the players, both male and female, as they practiced their layups and three-point shots. Among them, a young girl named Maya stood out, her determination and skill evident in every move she made. Maya had always loved playing basketball, but she knew that the sport meant much more to her than just a game. For Maya, basketball was a tool for promoting gender equality and breaking down barriers that had long restricted women's access to sports.

Maya had grown up in a community where girls were often discouraged from participating in sports. It was seen as a "boys' activity," and girls were expected to focus on more "feminine" pursuits. However, Maya refused to conform to these outdated stereotypes. She had seen firsthand the power of sports to empower and uplift women, and she was determined to make a difference in her own community.

As Maya honed her skills on the basketball court, she began to notice the impact that her presence was having on the other girls in her school. They would come to watch her play, and some even expressed their desire to join the team. Maya knew that she had become a symbol of possibility for these girls, showing them that they too could excel in a traditionally male-dominated sport.

Inspired by Maya's example, a group of girls approached the school administration and advocated for the creation of a girls' basketball team. At first, they faced resistance and skepticism, but Maya and her friends refused to be discouraged. They organized a petition, gathered support from teachers and parents, and made their case for the importance of providing equal opportunities for girls in sports.

Their hard work paid off, and soon enough, the school announced the formation of a girls' basketball team. Maya and her friends were overjoyed, knowing that they had paved the way for future generations of girls to pursue their athletic dreams. The team quickly gained popularity, drawing in girls from diverse backgrounds and skill levels. Maya embraced her role as a mentor and leader, guiding her teammates with patience and encouragement.

As the girls' basketball team flourished, Maya began to see the ripple effects of their success throughout the school and the broader community. Other sports teams started to become more inclusive, welcoming girls who had previously felt excluded. The school administration implemented policies to ensure equal access to sports facilities and resources for all students, regardless of gender. Even outside of school, Maya noticed a shift in attitudes towards girls in sports, with more and more families encouraging their daughters to pursue athletic interests.

The impact of sports on promoting gender equality was clear to Maya, and she was determined to continue her advocacy beyond the basketball court. She became involved in organizing workshops and events to raise awareness about the importance of girls' participation in sports, speaking at local community gatherings and writing articles for the school newspaper. Maya also sought out mentors and role models in the sports industry, connecting with female athletes and leaders who shared her passion for breaking down gender barriers.

Through her efforts, Maya began to see a gradual shift in attitudes and perceptions towards girls in sports. The once-male-dominated sports culture was becoming more inclusive and diverse, with girls and women taking their place alongside their male counterparts. Maya knew that there was still much work to be done, but she felt hopeful and empowered by the progress she had witnessed.

As Maya reflected on her journey, she realized that sports had the power to transcend gender stereotypes and promote equality in profound ways. The teamwork, discipline, and resilience that she had learned on the basketball court had shaped her into a confident and empowered young woman, ready to take on any challenge that came her way. Maya knew that she would continue to be a champion for gender equality in sports, using her passion for basketball as a catalyst for change in her community and beyond.

Title: The Incredible Floating Card Trick

Introduction:
Welcome to the world of magic! Today, I will teach you how to perform an incredible floating card trick that will leave your audience amazed. This trick is not only visually stunning but also deceptively simple and easy to learn. Are you ready? Let's begin!

Materials:
1. A deck of cards
2. A table
3. A spectator's assistance

Preparation:
Begin by having your audience sit around a table with you in the center. Shuffle the deck of cards and place it face down on the table. Make sure the deck is spread out so that everyone can see it clearly.

The Trick:
Now, invite a spectator to assist you in the trick. This person will be responsible for holding the deck of cards during the performance. Have the spectator place their hand gently on top of the deck, palm down, and slightly spread out. Make sure the deck is still facing downward and that the spectator is holding it firmly.

Next, you will proceed to "cut" the deck of cards into two halves by placing your thumb between the two halves and separating them. However, instead of actually cutting the deck, you will subtly shift your thumb to the side and bring the halves closer together, making it appear as if you have cut the deck cleanly.

Once the deck is cut, you will ask the spectator to "choose" any card from either half of the deck. Make sure they know they can pick any card they want. Encourage them to look at the card carefully and remember its position within the deck.

Now, you will proceed to "reverse" the deck by placing your hand on top and pushing down gently. As you do this, the spectator will be asked to lift the bottom half of the deck slightly. This action will create the illusion that the deck is reversing itself, with the chosen card now ending up at the bottom.

Once the deck is reversed, you will ask the spectator to remove the deck from your hand and place it face down on the table. At this point, the deck should still be spread out slightly, and the chosen card should be at the bottom.

The Finale:
Next, you will ask the spectator to gently tap the deck twice, lightly shuffling the cards. After the shuffle, you will have them spread out the deck again and look for their chosen card, which should be face up at the bottom.

When the spectator finds their card, you will ask them to "float" the card by gently lifting it from the bottom of the deck. As the spectator attempts to lift the card, you will secretly push down on the top half of the deck to make it appear as if the card is levitating above the deck.

Once the card is floating about 1-2 inches above the deck, you will have the spectator place it back on top of the deck and spread it out again. You will then ask them to "float" the card once more, but this time, they should try to push it away from themselves instead of pulling it towards them.

As the spectator pushes the card away, you will again secretly push down on the top half of the deck, making it seem like the card is being repelled by the deck. After a brief moment, the spectator should be able to successfully float the card away from themselves.触

The sundial, an ancient timekeeping device that has captivated the imaginations of humans for millennia, stands as a testament to our enduring fascination with the passage of time. Its history is intertwined with the development of human civilization, from the earliest civilizations of Egypt and Mesopotamia to the sophisticated societies of Greece and Rome.

The sundial's origins can be traced back to the early civilizations of Egypt and Mesopotamia, where the movement of the sun across the sky was observed and recorded. These early sundials were simple in design, consisting of a stick or obelisk placed vertically in the ground. The shadow cast by the object would indicate the time of day based on its position in relation to the sun.

As civilizations advanced, so did the sophistication of sundials. The ancient Egyptians developed more complex sundials, such as the shadow clocks, which utilized a series of markings on a flat surface to indicate the time. These sundials were often aligned with the cardinal points of the compass, allowing for more accurate timekeeping.

The Greeks and Romans made significant advancements in sundial technology. They introduced the use of gnomons, which were pointers that cast shadows onto the sundial's markings. This allowed for greater precision in timekeeping, and sundials became an integral part of daily life. Sundials were used to regulate public events, agricultural activities, and even religious ceremonies.

One of the most famous sundials from antiquity is the Tower of the Winds in Athens, Greece. Built in the 1st century BC, this octagonal tower featured sundials on each of its eight sides, allowing for timekeeping throughout the day. The tower also served as a weather vane and a public meeting place, demonstrating the sundial's importance in both practical and social aspects of life.

Despite the advent of more advanced timekeeping devices, such as mechanical clocks and watches, sundials continued to be used throughout history. Their simplicity, reliability, and connection to the natural world ensured their enduring popularity. Sundials were often incorporated into public spaces, gardens, and architectural structures as decorative elements, serving as reminders of the timeless nature of time.

In the modern era, sundials have evolved into more than just timekeeping instruments. They have become symbols of history, art, and scientific curiosity. Many ancient sundials are preserved as cultural artifacts, offering a glimpse into the ingenuity and creativity of past civilizations.

The sundial's enduring legacy lies in its ability to connect us to the past while reminding us of the ever-flowing nature of time. As we marvel at the intricate designs and precise craftsmanship of ancient sundials, we are transported to a world where time was measured by the movement of the sun and the ingenuity of human minds.

This year's award was won jointly by Ellen Johnson Sirleaf, the president of Liberia, Leymah Gbowee, the Liberian peace activist, and Yemeni pro-democracy campaigner Tawakkol Karman. They were recognised for their non-violent struggle for the safety of women and for women's rights to full participation in peace-building work. Leymah Gbowee, 39, is a Liberian social worker and peace activist who has built a peace movement by training and organising women to challenge Liberia's warlords. She is the founder of Women of Liberia Mass Action for Peace, an organisation that has brought together Christian and Muslim women in a nonviolent movement that played a pivotal role in ending Liberia's civil war. Leymah Gbowee mobilised and organised Christian and Muslim women across ethnic and religious dividing lines to demonstrate together, confronting Liberia's ruthless president and rebel warlords, and even held a sex strike. The women's mass movement helped to bring an end to the war in 2003. Gbowee has also mobilised women to participate in the elections and the peace process, and in post-conflict reconstruction. Leymah Gbowee is an exceptional woman in many ways. At 39, she is one of the youngest laureates of the Peace Prize. She has also made herself heard in a country and a region where women traditionally have been excluded from politics and decision-making. The women's peace movement is the vanguard of a new women's movement in Africa, and a triumph for African women's participation in the peace and reconciliation process. The Norwegian Nobel Committee has wished to honour women who have shown extraordinary courage and taken personal risks. The Committee sees this as an important contribution to peace. The Prize is also intended as a message to women all over the world that they - despite the often difficult conditions - can play an active part in peace work. Leymah Gbowee, Ellen Johnson Sirleaf and Tawakkol Karman are the three women laureates since 2004, when the Committee decided to award half of the Prize to Wangari Muta Maathai. Since the year 2000, four of the prizes have been awarded to women. The Nobel Peace Prize 2011 has been awarded to three women for their non-violent struggle for the safety of women and for women's rights to full participation in peace-building work. We congratulate the laureates and are proud that a Norwegian is among them. The Committee has also decided to award the Prize to the three women in order to bring attention to the discrimination women in many countries experience in peacetime. Ellen Johnson Sirleaf has, ever since she became president in Liberia, contributed to securing peace in her country. She has supported peace processes in the region, promoted economic and social development, and has strengthened the position of women. Tawakkul Karman has played a leading part in the struggle for women's rights and for democracy and peace in Yemen. Randy was a father of two mischievous kids, Jack and Lily. They loved playing pranks on each other and on their friends. Randy had always warned them not to play pranks on strangers or anyone who could get hurt from their tricks. One day, Randy came up with an idea to trick his kids. He had been trying to teach them a lesson about being too trusting, and he knew just how to do it. "Hey Jack, Lily, I want to show you guys something," Randy said, "but you have to promise not to tell anyone." "What is it, dad?" Jack asked, intrigued. "It's a surprise," Randy replied. "But first, I need you guys to close your eyes and count to 10. When you open your eyes, something magical will happen." Excited, the kids closed their eyes and began counting. As soon as the kids closed their eyes, Randy quickly changed his shirt, put on a mask and hid behind a nearby bush. When the kids opened their eyes, they were shocked to see a stranger in front of them. The stranger was wearing a mask and held a bag of candy that he offered to the kids. "Hi there, little ones," the stranger said with a smile. "I have some candy for you. Would you like some?" The kids were hesitant at first, but the stranger was persuasive. Randy watched from his hiding spot, waiting for his kids to come to their senses. Suddenly, Jack spoke up. "Wait a minute," he said, "you're not our dad! You're just someone pretending to be!" Randy jumped out from behind the bush, laughing. "Gotcha!" he said. "I wanted to teach you guys a lesson about trusting strangers. You never know who you're talking to or what their intentions are." The kids were relieved and a little embarrassed. "You tricked us, dad!" Lily said, crossing her arms. "I know," Randy said. "But it was for your own good. Now promise me you'll never trust strangers again." Jack and Lily nodded, both a little wiser now. They knew their dad would always be there to teach them important life lessons, even if it meant tricking them a little.
