The Neonatal Sepsis Concept Term Paper

Table of Contents
 1. Introduction
 2. Background
 3. Literature Review
 4. Conclusion
 5. References

Introduction

The majority of medical practitioners and organizations specializing in the delivery of healthcare are concerned about the increased rate of mortality and morbidity among infants and mothers. For this reason, measures have been taken to ensure the reduction of child and maternal mortality rates. For instance, a study carried out by Bishai et al. (2016), showed that such rates have reduced from 43% in 1990 to 40% in 2010, which was attributable to the improvement in education, governance, income, technology, societal changes, and better healthcare. In spite of this, empirical evidence shows that neonatal sepsis adversely affects the efforts taken to ensure reduced cases of child and maternal mortality especially in developing countries. This paper provides an in-depth analysis of the subject of neonatal sepsis.

Background

Neonatal sepsis can be either early-onset or late-onset. In the majority of the cases, early-onset sepsis occurs following the possibility of the baby having acquired various microorganisms from the mother (Shah & Padbury, 2013). Some of the common microorganisms responsible for this category of sepsis include Escherichia coli , coagulase-negative Staphylococcus, Group B Streptococcus (GBS), Listeria monocytogenes , and Haemophilus influenzae . In spite of this, the prevalence of sepsis due to GBS has reduced over time because of the use of prenatal screening as well as other treatment protocol for Group B Streptococcus.

On the other hand, the late-onset sepsis develops later after a child is born, between 4 to 90 days. Often, this category of sepsis results from the caregiving environmental conditions. While a newborn is exposed to numerous microorganisms that can trigger sepsis, the Coagulase-negative Staphylococcus is known to be the major cause of neonatal sepsis.

Literature Review

Neonatal sepsis has been identified as a leading cause of term and preterm infants’ morbidity and mortality (Gebremedhin, Berhe, & Gebrekirstos, 2016; Bishai et al., 2016). In spite of the various measures taken to ensure advanced neonatal care, sepsis still accounts for a significant percentage of morbidity and mortality in infants having very low weight at birth. Neonatal sepsis’s signs and symptoms are not specific (Shah & Padbury, 2013). However, the most common ones experienced in children with sepsis include guaiac-positive stool, hepatomegaly, abdominal distention, bleeding problems, poor perfusion, bulging fontanel, seizures, hypotonia, irritability, feeding difficulties, apnea, and cyanosis among others.

The prevention and treatment of neonatal sepsis is challenging especially in developing countries. A study by Gebremedhin et al. (2016) indicated that the majority of the deaths of newborns in Ethiopia occur due to sepsis. In most of the cases, Gebremedhin et al. (2016) found out that such deaths are associated with factors such as the place of delivery, low birth weight, prematurity, prolonged rupture of membrane (PROM) and intrapartum fever, and the history of UTI/STI during the index pregnancy.

According to PATH (2015), it is recommedable to use either intravenous or intramuscular antibiotics for the treatment of neonatal sepsis. Nevertheless, such guidelines have not been useful since most of the healthcare settings lack hospital-based care. On the other hand, the World Health Organization (WHO) recommends the adoption of an outpatient treatment scheme to reduce child and maternal mortality rate due to neonatal sepsis. According to a study carried out by PATH (2015), it is possible to reduce infant deaths through the use of gentamicin. In spite of this, the only challenge in this case, would be the calculation of dosage.

Recent studies on neonatal sepsis have indicated that the examination of each category of sepsis can be effective in its prevention and treatment (Shah & Padbury, 2013; Schlapbach et al., 2011). As such, following the adoption and implementation of treatment protocol and prenatal screening, the prevalence rate of early-onset sepsis has decreased. The early detection as well as prompt treatment of neonatal sepsis remains to be a challenge due to the fact that the associated symptoms and signs of this illness are nonspecific. Numerous studies have been conducted to identify a number of diagnostic markers such as the cell surface markers, cytokines, procalcitonin, hematological indices, C-reactive protein, and acute phase reactants among others, which can be used in the detection of the signs and symptoms of neonatal sepsis (Shah & Padbury, 2013). In spite of this, there is a need for further researcher to establish a biomarker that is highly accurate.

Conclusion

Based on the analysis above, it is evident that child and maternal mortality is a common problem in healthcare nowadays. While interventions have been adopted to reduce the rate of morbidity and mortality rates of infants, neonatal sepsis has adversely affected such efforts. This is attributable to the fact that sepsis’s symptoms are nonspecific making their early detection and treatment a challenge. The adoption of technology in the healthcare sector has significantly increased the success rate regarding the prevention and treatment of neonatal sepsis. In spite of this, there is still much to be done to efficiently deal with this problem since more accurate and valid markers for the detection of signs and symptoms of neonatal sepsis are yet to be developed.

Artificial intelligence and transhumanism have been popular themes in science fiction literature and film for decades. These concepts delve into the possibilities and implications of advanced technology and the potential for human enhancement. Works like I, Robot, Ex Machina, Her, and Westworld offer diverse and thought-provoking portrayals of these ideas, each presenting unique perspectives on the intersection of humanity and technology.

In I, Robot, a collection of short stories by Isaac Asimov, the portrayal of artificial intelligence revolves around the concept of the Three Laws of Robotics, which are programmed into robots to ensure their behavior aligns with human ethics. The stories explore the complexities and potential consequences of these laws, as well as the evolving relationship between humans and robots. Asimov's work raises questions about the ethical implications of creating intelligent machines and the potential for coexistence between humans and artificial beings.

Similarly, Ex Machina delves into the ethical and existential implications of artificial intelligence through the character of Ava, a highly advanced humanoid robot. The film examines the nature of consciousness and the blurred lines between human and machine, as Ava demonstrates signs of self-awareness and autonomy. The portrayal of artificial intelligence in Ex Machina raises profound questions about the nature of humanity and the potential for sentient machines to experience emotions and desires.

On the other hand, the film Her offers a more intimate exploration of artificial intelligence, focusing on the relationship between a man and an operating system with advanced AI. The story delves into themes of loneliness, intimacy, and the potential for emotional connections between humans and artificial beings. By portraying the AI as a complex and emotionally intelligent entity, Her challenges traditional perceptions of artificial intelligence and invites audiences to consider the nature of consciousness and the potential for meaningful relationships with non-human entities.

In the television series Westworld, the portrayal of artificial intelligence is intertwined with the concept of transhumanism, which explores the potential for human enhancement through advanced technology. The show depicts a futuristic theme park populated by lifelike androids, blurring the lines between human and machine. Westworld raises thought-provoking questions about the nature of identity, free will, and the ethical implications of creating beings with human-like consciousness. Through its portrayal of transhumanism, the series challenges viewers to consider the potential consequences of pushing the boundaries of human enhancement and the integration of technology into the human experience.

Overall, the works I, Robot, Ex Machina, Her, and Westworld offer diverse and compelling portrayals of artificial intelligence and transhumanism, each presenting unique perspectives on the intersections of humanity and technology. Through these narratives, audiences are invited to contemplate the ethical, existential, and philosophical implications of advanced technology and its potential to reshape the human experience. As society continues to advance technologically, these works serve as poignant reflections on the complex relationship between humanity and the ever-evolving world of artificial intelligence and transhumanism.

The poem "Do Not Go Gentle into That Good Night" by Dylan Thomas is a powerful and emotional piece that explores the theme of fighting against death. The poem is a villanelle, which is a fixed-form poem with 19 lines and a specific rhyme scheme. The repetition of certain lines and phrases adds to the urgency and intensity of the poem. In this paper, I will analyze the poem and explain how literary devices are used to convey the message of fighting against the inevitability of death.
One of the most prominent literary devices used in the poem is the use of metaphor. The phrase "that good night" is a metaphor for death, and the speaker is urging the reader not to go gently into it. This metaphor is reinforced throughout the poem, with the speaker urging various types of people to fight against death. For example, in the first stanza, the speaker urges wise men to "rage" against the dying of the light, which is a metaphor for life. This metaphor is powerful because it suggests that life is like a light that is fading, and we should fight to keep it burning.
Another literary device used in the poem is repetition. The poem is a villanelle, which means that certain lines and phrases are repeated throughout the poem. This repetition adds to the urgency and intensity of the poem, as the speaker is repeating the same message over and over again. For example, the line "Do not go gentle into that good night" is repeated multiple times throughout the poem, and it becomes a refrain that reinforces the message of fighting against death.
The poem also uses imagery to convey its message. In the second stanza, the speaker urges wild men to "curse, bless, love, do anything," which is a powerful image that suggests that life is full of passion and emotion. This image is reinforced throughout the poem, as the speaker urges various types of people to fight against death with passion and intensity.
The use of alliteration is also prominent in the poem. For example, in the third stanza, the speaker urges "wise men" to "tear" their garments, which is a powerful image that suggests that life is like a garment that is being torn away. This image is reinforced by the use of alliteration, which adds to the intensity of the message.
In conclusion, "Do Not Go Gentle into That Good Night" is a powerful and emotional poem that uses various literary devices to convey its message of fighting against the inevitability of death. The use of metaphor, repetition, imagery, and alliteration all add to the intensity of the poem, and they reinforce the message that life is precious and worth fighting for. The poem is a reminder that we should not go gentle into the night, but instead, we should fight to keep our lights burning bright.

The History of the Invention of the Battery

In the realm of technological advancements, the battery stands as one of the most important inventions in human history. A device that stores energy and converts it into a usable form to power various electronic devices, the battery has come a long way since its inception. This essay will explore the fascinating history of the invention of the battery, its evolution, and its impact on modern society.

The concept of a battery can be traced back to ancient civilizations, where early forms of electrical energy storage were used for various purposes such as lighting and medical treatments. However, it was not until the 18th and 19th centuries that the battery began to take shape as we know it today.

In 1748, German scientist Johann Siegmund Hahn is credited with creating the first-ever battery, known as the "Leiden Battery." The device consisted of a metal container filled with acid and connected to two different metals, which produced an electric current when submerged in the acid. This groundbreaking discovery laid the foundation for future developments in the field of electrochemistry.

Throughout the following decades, scientists and inventors continued to experiment with different materials and methods to improve the efficiency and capacity of these early batteries. In 1800, Italian physicist Alessandro Volta developed the first "voltaic pile," a series of metal disks separated by cardboard soaked in saltwater or acid. When connected in a circuit, these disks generated a steady flow of electricity, leading to the creation of the first "battery" in the modern sense of the term.

As the 19th century progressed, scientists like Michael Faraday and Georges Leclanché made significant contributions to the field of battery technology. Faraday invented the first primary cell, which used a porous potassium-sodium alloy as the anode and a moistened paper impregnated with acid as the cathode. Leclanché, on the other hand, developed the Leclanché cell, which used a mixture of potassium chloride and ammonium chloride as the electrolyte. These innovations led to the development of various types of batteries, including the dry cell and the rechargeable battery.

The 20th century saw the widespread adoption of batteries in various applications, from radios and televisions to portable electronics and electric vehicles. The development of new materials and manufacturing techniques allowed for the creation of smaller, more powerful, and longer-lasting batteries. One of the most significant milestones in battery technology during this period was the invention of the nickel-cadmium battery by Waldemar Jungner in 1919. This type of battery was widely used in industrial and military applications due to its high energy density and long lifespan.

In recent decades, the focus has shifted towards developing batteries that are more efficient, environmentally friendly, and cost-effective. Lithium-ion batteries have emerged as the most popular choice for portable electronics and electric vehicles due to their high energy density, lightweight design, and long lifespan. Researchers continue to explore new materials and techniques to improve the performance of these batteries and reduce their environmental impact.

In conclusion, the history of the invention of the battery is a testament to human ingenuity and the relentless pursuit of technological advancements. From its humble beginnings in ancient civilizations to its current status as a crucial component in modern society, the battery has undoubtedly played a significant role in shaping the course of human progress. As research and development in this field continue, the future holds great promise for even more innovative and efficient batteries that will power our lives in ways we can only imagine.

In the vast expanse of the universe, there exists a myriad of celestial bodies, each with its unique characteristics and properties. Among these celestial wonders, the sun stands out as a colossal, luminous sphere of gas that sustains life on Earth. Our sun, a G-type main-sequence star, is approximately 4.6 billion years old and is positioned at the center of our solar system. It is a massive ball of plasma, composed primarily of hydrogen and helium, with a diameter of about 1.4 million kilometers. The sun's immense gravitational force holds the solar system together, with all the planets, moons, asteroids, and other celestial objects orbiting around it in a harmonious dance.

The sun's life cycle began when a massive cloud of gas and dust, known as a nebula, collapsed under its own gravity, leading to the formation of a protostar. As the protostar accumulated more mass, the pressure and temperature at its core increased, ultimately leading to nuclear fusion. This process, which has been ongoing for the past 4.6 billion years, converts hydrogen into helium through a series of nuclear reactions, releasing a tremendous amount of energy in the form of light and heat.

This energy emanating from the sun is essential for life on Earth, as it provides the necessary warmth and light for photosynthesis, the process by which plants convert sunlight into chemical energy. The sun's energy also drives the Earth's climate, influencing weather patterns and the distribution of life across the planet.

Apart from its role in sustaining life, the sun has also played a significant part in human history and culture. Ancient civilizations, such as the Egyptians and the Mayans, worshipped the sun as a symbol of life, fertility, and power. Solar deities were revered and honored through rituals and sacrifices, reflecting the sun's crucial role in their agricultural cycles.

However, our relationship with the sun is not without its challenges. Solar activity, including sunspots, solar flares, and coronal mass ejections, can have detrimental effects on Earth's technology and communication systems. Solar storms can disrupt power grids, damage satellites, and even pose a risk to astronauts in space. As our society becomes increasingly reliant on technology, understanding and mitigating the impacts of solar activity becomes ever more important.

In recent years, there has been a growing interest in harnessing the sun's energy through solar power. Photovoltaic cells, which convert sunlight directly into electricity, have become more efficient and affordable, making solar power a viable alternative to fossil fuels. Solar energy is not only renewable but also produces significantly fewer greenhouse gas emissions than traditional power sources, making it a crucial component in the fight against climate change.

As we continue to explore the cosmos, our understanding of the sun and its role in the universe only deepens. Future missions, such as NASA's Parker Solar Probe, are designed to study the sun up close, shedding light on its inner workings and providing critical information for our ongoing quest to understand the cosmos.

In conclusion, the sun is an awe-inspiring celestial body that has shaped our planet, our history, and our very existence. Its life-sustaining energy is essential for life on Earth, and its influence stretches far beyond our own world, affecting the entire solar system and beyond. As we continue to explore and learn more about our sun, we deepen our appreciation for this magnificent star and the role it plays in our lives and our universe.

Sustainable architecture plays a crucial role in building design as it focuses on creating environmentally friendly, energy-efficient, and socially responsible structures. This approach to architecture takes into consideration the environmental impact of the building materials, energy usage, and overall design to minimize the negative effects on the planet. Sustainable architecture not only benefits the environment but also contributes to the health and well-being of the occupants, as well as the surrounding community.

One of the key aspects of sustainable architecture is the use of environmentally friendly building materials. This includes materials that are renewable, recycled, or have a low impact on the environment. For example, using wood from sustainably managed forests, recycled steel, and low-emission concrete can significantly reduce the carbon footprint of a building. Additionally, the use of non-toxic materials and finishes can improve indoor air quality, creating a healthier living and working environment for the occupants.

In building design, sustainable architecture also emphasizes energy efficiency. This involves incorporating passive design strategies such as orientation, shading, natural ventilation, and insulation to reduce the need for artificial heating and cooling. Furthermore, the integration of energy-efficient systems and technologies, such as solar panels, geothermal heating, and LED lighting, can further minimize the building's energy consumption and reliance on non-renewable resources.

Moreover, sustainable architecture promotes water conservation through the implementation of water-efficient fixtures, rainwater harvesting systems, and greywater recycling. By reducing water usage, buildings can lessen their impact on local water sources and contribute to the overall conservation of this valuable resource. Additionally, sustainable architecture considers the management of stormwater runoff to prevent pollution and erosion, thus maintaining the ecological balance of the surrounding area.

In terms of the social impact, sustainable architecture aims to create buildings that are accessible, inclusive, and contribute positively to the community. This involves designing spaces that are adaptable to the needs of diverse users, including people with disabilities, the elderly, and children. Furthermore, sustainable architecture encourages the integration of green spaces, public transportation access, and pedestrian-friendly designs to promote a sense of community and reduce the reliance on private vehicles.

The role of sustainable architecture in building design extends beyond the construction phase and encompasses the entire life cycle of the building. This includes considering the potential for deconstruction, reuse, and recycling of materials at the end of the building's life. By designing for disassembly and incorporating reusable materials, sustainable architecture promotes a circular economy and minimizes the amount of waste sent to landfills.

Furthermore, sustainable architecture encourages a holistic approach to building design that takes into account the cultural, historical, and ecological context of the site. By respecting the natural landscape and local traditions, sustainable buildings can seamlessly integrate into their surroundings, enhancing the overall sense of place and identity.

In conclusion, sustainable architecture plays a vital role in building design by prioritizing environmental responsibility, energy efficiency, and social impact. By incorporating environmentally friendly materials, energy-efficient systems, water conservation measures, and community-oriented designs, sustainable architecture contributes to a more sustainable and resilient built environment. As the demand for sustainable building practices continues to grow, the role of sustainable architecture will only become more significant in shaping the future of our cities and communities.

Jay got a job out of state. He had one month left in his lease. Jay's lease came up for renewal. He talked to his landlord. Jay let the lease go on to the next tenant. He agreed to keep paying rent until the new tenant moved in. He also agreed to take care of the place and not tear it up. Jay's landlord allowed him to use the same security deposit for the new tenant. A security deposit is money a tenant pays a landlord. The landlord holds the security deposit to pay for damage. The tenant does not pay rent with the deposit. The landlord must return the security deposit when the tenant moves out. The landlord can keep all or part of the deposit. The landlord must give a written list of damages. The landlord must give the written list within 30 days. The landlord must return the rest of the deposit. Jay had paid a security deposit of 500. He had not damaged the place. He had paid the rent on time. The landlord agreed to let Jay use the same security deposit for the new tenant. Jay left the rental unit clean and undamaged. He moved out one week before the new tenant moved in. The landlord sent Jay a written list of damages. It showed 300 in damages. The landlord kept 300 from Jay's deposit. Jay was upset. He felt the landlord was wrong. He had not damaged the rental unit. Jay contacted the Utah Apartment Association. Jay learned the landlord had done nothing wrong. The landlord had agreed to let Jay use the same security deposit. The agreement did not say the landlord had to return all of the deposit. It only said that the landlord would take the deposit from the new tenant. Jay should have asked the landlord for a written agreement. It would have said the landlord would give back Jay's deposit. It would also have said the landlord would not keep any of the deposit.

Planning and Implementing Organizational Development Interventions Essay

Organizational development (OD) is an integral part of any enterprises’ work wishing to remain successful and competitively capable. OD is a scientifically based process that focuses on various aspects and work processes to improve the organization’s effectiveness (van Vulpen, 2020). To make the necessary changes, interventions are carried out – several activities to implement the desired changes. Given the importance of such changes and the fact that they should be based on scientific evidence, OD interventions require careful preparation and thought-out planning and implementation.

Preparation for OD interventions includes developing a strategy, in particular, such steps as:

  * diagnosis,
  * determining the structure of interventions,
  * choosing and establishing sequencing,
  * taking into account the dynamics of intervention,
  * considering the expected result.

If a problem is identified or the administration wants to make a change, it is necessary to find out whether the desired shift is suitable for the work of the organization. Moreover, it is crucial to determine employees’ readiness and calculate the necessary time, resources, and efforts. When defining the structure of interventions, it is essential to analyze such aspects as stakeholders, clarity of purpose, the realism of expectations, employees’ readiness to study and work together.

The sequencing of interventions also depends on several crucial factors. For example, it is affected by potential efficiency – if an organization needs to motivate employees to make changes, this OD intervention should be the first. The manager must also view what sequence will keep the resources, contribute to the rapid speed of changes, be more relevant to the organization and create minimal stress for employees. According to French and Bell (1999), interventions have different dynamics depending on their types, such as the dilemma intervention, respective intervention, and other kinds. It is critical to ensure that the selected type matches the desired change. Finally, intervention depends on the expected result – for example, the goal may be to educate employees or increase motivation and efficiency.

Thus, OD interventions are designed to improve and optimize the enterprise’s operation through a number of actions. In order for the intervention to be effective, many critical factors must be taken into account in its planning and implementation. In particular, it is crucial to consider the circumstances, goals, and dynamics. Careful preparation will determine the strategy, structure, time, and resources required, making intervention fast and beneficial.

In a world where trust is often scarce, the need for transparency and traceability in supply chains has become more important than ever. The blockchain technology has emerged as a powerful tool that can help achieve this much-needed transparency, providing a secure and decentralized platform for recording transactions and tracking products throughout their journey from the manufacturer to the consumer.

Our story begins in a bustling global marketplace, where a myriad of goods are traded every day. The supply chain of these products is a complex web of interconnected parties, each playing a vital role in the creation, distribution, and sale of the final product. However, this intricate web also presents a significant challenge: ensuring the transparency and traceability of each product, allowing consumers to make informed decisions about the items they purchase.

Let's consider a hypothetical scenario that illustrates the role of blockchain in supply chain transparency and traceability. Imagine a large multinational corporation that manufactures a popular line of organic, fair-trade coffee beans. The company prides itself on its commitment to sustainability, and its coffee beans are sourced from small-scale farmers in remote regions around the world. The coffee beans are then roasted, packaged, and shipped to retailers worldwide.

Now, let's delve into the supply chain of this coffee bean, starting with the farmers who harvest the cherries from which the beans are derived. The farmers belong to a cooperative that ensures fair trade practices and sustainable farming methods are maintained. The cherries are then processed and dried, after which they are transported to a local warehouse for storage.

To maintain transparency and traceability, each batch of coffee cherries is assigned a unique identifier, such as a barcode or QR code. This identifier is then recorded on a blockchain ledger, which serves as a permanent, immutable, and transparent record of the transactions and events in the supply chain.

The blockchain ledger is shared among all the participants in the supply chain, from the farmers to the retailers. This means that each party can verify the authenticity of the coffee beans at each stage of the supply chain, ensuring that the beans have been sourced from the correct farmers and that the necessary quality controls have been met.

As the coffee beans are processed, roasted, packaged, and shipped to retailers, the blockchain ledger is updated with the relevant information and transactions. This creates an auditable trail of the product's journey, allowing consumers to trace the coffee beans back to their source and verify the authenticity of the product.

Furthermore, the use of blockchain technology in the supply chain can also help to prevent counterfeit products from entering the market. By creating a transparent and immutable record of the product's journey, consumers can be assured that the coffee beans they purchase are genuine and have not been tampered with or substituted with inferior products.

The implementation of blockchain technology in the supply chain is not without its challenges, however. The adoption of new technologies requires significant investment in infrastructure, training, and integration with existing systems. Additionally, the security and privacy of the blockchain data must be ensured, as well as the scalability of the platform to accommodate the growing demand.

Despite these challenges, the potential benefits of blockchain technology in achieving supply chain transparency and traceability are immense. By enabling consumers to trace the products they purchase back to their source, the technology empowers informed decision-making and helps to build trust in the global marketplace.

In conclusion, the role of blockchain in supply chain transparency and traceability is a critical factor in the modern economy. By providing a secure and transparent platform for recording transactions and tracking products throughout their journey, the technology enables consumers to make informed decisions about the products they purchase, fostering trust and integrity in the global marketplace.

Some scientific studies suggest that ozone depletion may have a dominant role in governing climatic change in Antarctica (and a wider area of the Southern Hemisphere). Ozone absorbs large amounts of ultraviolet radiation in the stratosphere. Ozone depletion over Antarctica can cause a cooling of around 6 C in the local stratosphere. This cooling has the effect of intensifying the westerly winds which flow around the continent (the polar vortex) and thus prevents outflow of the cold air near the South Pole. As a result, the continental mass of the East Antarctic ice sheet is held at lower temperatures, and the peripheral areas of Antarctica, especially the Antarctic Peninsula, are subject to higher temperatures, which promote accelerated melting. Models also suggest that the ozone depletionenhanced polar vortex effect also accounts for the recent increase in sea ice just offshore of the continent.

In today's world, media literacy has become an essential skill for promoting civic engagement. Civic engagement refers to the active participation of individuals in their communities and societies to make a positive impact. Media literacy, on the other hand, is the ability to critically analyze, evaluate, and create media content. It is the ability to understand the underlying messages, motives, and impact of media on society. The importance of media literacy in promoting civic engagement cannot be overstated.

Firstly, media literacy empowers individuals to be more informed about the issues affecting their communities. With the proliferation of media outlets and the ease of access to information, it has become increasingly difficult for individuals to discern between fact and fiction. Media literacy equips individuals with the skills to critically evaluate the credibility of sources and to analyze the content they consume. By being better informed, individuals are more likely to participate in civic activities that are meaningful to them.

Secondly, media literacy encourages individuals to engage in constructive dialogue about social issues. Media has the power to shape public opinion and influence social norms. However, media content is often biased or one-sided, which can lead to misunderstandings and conflicts. By learning how to critically analyze media content, individuals can identify these biases and engage in constructive dialogue about social issues. This can lead to more informed decision-making and effective policy solutions.

Thirdly, media literacy empowers individuals to create their own media content. In today's digital age, individuals have the power to create and share their own stories and opinions through social media platforms, blogs, and other online platforms. By learning how to create media content, individuals can become active participants in shaping public discourse. This can lead to more diverse voices being heard and can help to challenge traditional power structures.

Lastly, media literacy promotes civic engagement by fostering a sense of civic responsibility. By understanding the role of media in society, individuals are more likely to recognize their responsibility to participate in civic life. This can lead to greater participation in elections, volunteering, and other forms of civic engagement.

In conclusion, media literacy is crucial in promoting civic engagement. It empowers individuals to be more informed, engage in constructive dialogue, create their own media content, and fosters a sense of civic responsibility. Therefore, it is essential that we invest in media literacy education to ensure that our citizens are equipped to participate effectively in democracy.

The Importance of Diversity in the Workplace

Diversity is an important aspect in the workplace, as it brings people from different backgrounds, cultures, and experiences together to work towards a common goal. A workplace that embraces diversity is more likely to be innovative, creative, and productive. It is also an organization that values the opinions, perspectives, and contributions of all employees.

One of the key benefits of diversity in the workplace is innovation. People from different backgrounds often have different experiences and ideas, which can lead to unique perspectives. When these perspectives are shared and valued, it can lead to new ideas and solutions that may not have been considered before. This is particularly important in today's fast-paced and ever-changing business environment.

Another benefit of diversity is the ability to connect with a wide range of customers. In today's global market, businesses need to be able to connect with customers from different backgrounds and cultures. A diverse workforce can help companies better understand and serve their customers by providing a variety of perspectives and experiences. This can lead to increased customer loyalty and satisfaction.

Furthermore, diversity can lead to improved employee engagement and retention. Employees who feel valued and appreciated for their unique perspectives and contributions are more likely to be engaged in their work and less likely to leave the organization. Diversity also fosters a sense of belongingness, which can lead to increased job satisfaction and motivation.

However, creating a diverse workplace is not without its challenges. One of the biggest challenges is unconscious bias. Unconscious bias refers to the automatic and often unintentional attitudes and stereotypes that people form about others based on their background. These biases can lead to discrimination and can prevent people from being hired or promoted based on their merit.

Another challenge is cultural competence. Cultural competence refers to the ability of an individual or organization to interact effectively with people from different cultures. This involves understanding and respecting different cultures, as well as being aware of one's own culture and how it may impact interactions with others.

To overcome these challenges, organizations need to implement diversity and inclusion training for employees. This training should help employees recognize and understand their own biases and how they may impact their interactions with others. It should also provide them with tools and strategies to work effectively in diverse teams.

In conclusion, diversity in the workplace is essential for innovation, customer connection, employee engagement, and overall business success. While creating a diverse workplace can be challenging, it is a necessary step towards building a more inclusive and equitable future. By fostering a culture of respect and appreciation for all employees, organizations can create a workplace where everyone feels valued and can contribute their best work.

Introduction

Mobile phones, which were invented a few decades ago, have become important communication devices utilized by society members of all ages. One age group that has made persistent use of mobile phones is teenagers. Teenagers’ overuse of phones has had a marked effect on their school lives. This paper will address the negative impacts that mobile phones are having on teenagers’ school life.

Negative Impacts

Mobile phones impose financial pressures on teenagers since these devices act as status symbol objects. Campbell (2005) confirms that most teenagers have the desire to upgrade their phones in order to fit in with their peers.

Since most teenagers do not have a source of income, they have to rely on their families to buy them phones and pay the phone bills. This raises issues of financial disputes and some teenagers end up stealing money from their parents to spend on their phones.

Teenagers use mobile phones to aid in cheating during exams. Students use their cell phones to communicate with each other during exams and therefore obtain answers to the test questions. Students can also cheat by getting answers from their phone memory or the internet.

Campbell (2005) documents that while teenagers have always engaged in cheating; mobile phones have increased the level of sophistication in cheating and decreased the chances of the misconduct being detected by the teacher.

Mobile phones are also problematic in school since they increase the level of disruption. Research indicates that teenagers are reluctant to switch off their phones while in class and this leads to learning activity being disrupted when the student receives a call or a text (Campbell, 2005).

Even when the student does not access his/her mobile phone, the excitement of finding out what the message is about results in the student losing interest in the class leading to poor academic outcomes.

Conclusion

Mobile phones have significant negative impacts on teenagers’ school life. This paper has demonstrated that mobile phones cause financial difficulties, enhance cheating, and disrupt lessons. Parents and teachers should therefore forbid teenagers from having mobile phones in school.

Reference

Campbell, M A 2005, The impact of the mobile phone on young people’s social life , Proceedings Social Change in the 21st Century Conference, QUT Carseldine, Brisbane.

Whenever I feel the urge to complain about something, these same words replay in my mind to remind me that I really have nothing to complain about. As I sit on my comfortable chair in the warmth of my apartment home and look out the foggy window to see the drops of rain rush down from the nighttime sky, I know that, at this very moment, there is an unfortunate human out there who struggles to find a dry place to sleep in and a way to keep from shivering. While someone out there has bigger problems to worry about, I only have to worry about things such as applying to college. I acknowledge that I am in a fortunate position and because of that, I believe it is my duty to give back to those who are not. The act of being grateful and giving back has become a big part of who I am today. I have come to realize that offering help to those who are less fortunate does not always mean that I must go out of my way. Simple acts such as donating unused clothes or handing over extra change to a needy person while treating higher with dignity allow me this. Recently, I have had the privilege of tutoring Robert, an "at-risk" juvenile. I helped him with homework assignments and got to know about him and his struggles with family and ADHD. I was able to step into the shoes of a mentor as I tried to show him the importance of education and having goals. My experience with helping others helps fill my life with purpose, a sense of righteousness, and serves as a reminder of how grateful I should be for where I am today. I know I am capable of making a positive impact in the Pepper dine community by bringing to the table a positive energy that is contagious and propels myself and those around me to stay focused on their goals and the well-being of others. Random acts of kindness towards others create lasting bonds which lead to a unified community with the shared goal of moving forward. By keeping my mother's words in mind, I plan to be the one to jump-start this trend.

The Zoraks, as they call themselves, make regular trips to visit us. As massive, hulking creatures with six limbs, they frequently run on our roads as a means of transport. When it's necessary for them to move on the pavement, they politely choose a bipedal stance to take up less space. They try not to shove us despite being the size of an SUV. Withing a week of the invasion our laws were rewritten. Life is peaceful. We still have jobs, but they're not nearly as stressful as, with Zoraki technology, resources have become plentiful. They're even reversing global warming for us. The language barrier was terrible at first. We were so confused about what they wanted to do and constantly afraid that they'd murder us for nor fulfilling their wishes. But in the end, it was they who learnt our social cues and gave us simple directions. They taught us basic words from their language, and we have (in a very human way) been starting to smith those words into our own languages. A few have even taken up the study of the Zoraki language, but it's a tiring and terribly complex subject. The strangest phenomenon, however, is when random Zoraks stop in the street, stare at a particular person, and start touching them. It's clearly not a sexual gesture. They mostly like to touch our hair and faces and sometimes hold hands. One would suppose it's because they don't have such a soft outer covering themselves. These interactions can be brief, lasting only a few minutes. Other times, when a Zorak takes a liking to a person, they'll invite them away for several weeks. These people always come back awestruck and happy with their experiences in whatever mothership or colony planet they visited. The bonds forged between alien and human can last for decades, with them coming to visit every few months and yearly trips to see the galaxy. Inevitably, it is the human who will die first. The Zoraks live for hundreds of years. At first it was strange seeing their hulking forms hunched over a human coffin, but over time we realised that their posture and low rumbling was indicative of sadness - the Zoraki form of crying. Their grief, however, does not last forever. Sometimes, after their preferred human passes, the Zorak will seek out that person's offspring and forge a new friendship. In short, most of us like our huge, tailed, alien overlords. There are a handful of dissenters, but there always are. What can you do, after all, but love them? They've provided for our every need and shown us affection when we don't have anything to offer in return. We are far from being as advanced as them and understanging them and yet, for some reason, they seem to genuinely enjoy our company.

Alpine plants such the Alpine gentian grow in abundance in areas such as the meadows above the Lauterbrunnental. Gentians are named after the Illyrian king Gentius, and 40 species of the early-spring blooming flower grow in the Alps, in a range of 1,500 to 2,400 m (4,921 to 7,874 ft). Writing about the gentians in Switzerland D. H. Lawrence described them as "darkening the day-time, torch-like with the smoking blueness of Pluto's gloom." Gentians tend to "appear" repeatedly as the spring blooming takes place at progressively later dates, moving from the lower altitude to the higher altitude meadows where the snow melts much later than in the valleys. On the highest rocky ledges the spring flowers bloom in the summer.

According to archaeologists and anthropologists, the earliest clothing likely consisted of fur, leather, leaves, or grass that were draped, wrapped, or tied around the body. Knowledge of such clothing remains inferential, since clothing materials deteriorate quickly compared to stone, bone, shell and metal artifacts. Archeologists have identified very early sewing needles of bone and ivory from about 30,000 BC, found near Kostenki, Russia in 1988. Dyed flax fibers that could have been used in clothing have been found in a prehistoric cave in the Republic of Georgia that date back to 36,000 BP.

Microbiology. Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Essay

Table of Contents
 1. Introduction
 2. Spreading the virus
 3. Signs and symptoms
 4. Test and diagnosis

 6. References

Introduction

Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome is one of the many viral respiratory diseases that emanate from the SARs coronavirus (Hui, Memish, & Zumla 2014). The disease originated in Southern China between late 2002 and mid-2003 (Hui, Memish, & Zumla 2014). At the onset of the disease outbreak, the immediate number of death cases amounted to 774. The disease affected 8,096 people including the number of deaths reported especially in Hong Kong (Hui, Memish, & Zumla 2014). Several other countries were also affected in the region.

Spreading the virus

Earlier on, coronavirus did not have such harmful effects on humans. The SARs strain has however changed this fact since its outbreak in 2002. The most notable spread of the disease is through the air (Yu, Qiu, Tse & Wong 2014). Therefore, the disease is faster spread through coughing, sneezing, and also breathing near an infected individual (Yu et at. 2014). Spreading the virus through personal contact with an infected person can be done through hugging, kissing, sharing utensils, and drinking from the same cup, direct touch, and proximity about 3 feet away from an infected person (Wildeman, Schnittker & Turney 2012).

Signs and symptoms

The disease is not contagious in its incubation period which lasts for about 2-7days (Yu et at. 2014). After the incubation period, in cases, the victim begins to experience a high fever. Alongside the fever, he or she experiences high temperatures and in most cases, it exceeds 38 degrees Celsius. In addition, the disease also has similar symptoms to those of the common flu. These symptoms include aches, chills as well as diarrhea (Yu et at. 2014). The victim may also experience very dry coughing and short breaths (Yu et at. 2014). Although at this point the symptoms are very mild, they further develop into more severe complications within a week. Such advanced complications include respiratory failure, heart failure as well as liver failure (Yu et at. 2014).

Test and diagnosis

There has not been a universal test that can specifically detect SARs. In fact, it is difficult to treat a patient who has been infected by SARs since there is no fast enough method to diagnose the treatment early enough. Normally, an infected person must have come into contact with a previously infected individual. Pneumonia is also a possible sign to diagnose a patient who is infected by SARs. (Cressoni et al. 2014). However, a patient is assumed to have SARs if he/she displays abnormal pneumonia.

Treatment and prevention

The treatment of SARs is similar to the treatment given for pneumonia especially the community-acquired atypical pneumonia (Franken, Ansems & Damink 2014). To prevent infections of the virus one should avoid physical contact with an infected person as well as avoiding sharing or contact of body fluids such as saliva and sweat. Basic personal hygiene is recommended in preventing the infection of SARs. This included washing your hands frequently, avoiding touching your mouth, and covering your mouth while coughing.

This paper describes our work on demonstrating verification technologies on a flight-critical system of realistic functionality, size, and complexity. Our work targeted a commercial aircraft control system named Transport Class Model (TCM), and involved several stages: formalizing and disambiguating requirements in collaboration with domain experts; processing models for their use by formal verification tools; applying compositional techniques at the architectural and component level to scale verification. Performed in the context of a major NASA milestone, this study of formal verification in practice is one of the most challenging that our group has performed, and it took several person months to complete it. This paper describes the methodology that we followed and the lessons that we learned.

Sears’ Mission and Vision Paper Report (Assessment)

Currently, vision and mission statements have been diluted in the business world to the extent that they have become less significant (Whiteley, 2007). As such, visions and missions have been mainly identified with unenthusiastic connotations. Nonetheless, when utilized appropriately vision and mission statements have proved to be very helpful.

Poorly structured vision and mission statements are misplaced opportunities for drawing and enhancing organizational culture, enhancing productivity, and drawing and preserving new talent. Researchers have shown that corporations that have distinct vision and mission statements that are supported with tactical strategies do better than those who do not (Whiteley, 2007).

Therefore, vision and mission statements offer organizations with bearing. Through this, corporations can be able to implement actions that guide their businesses forward and keep away from allocating capital to actions that do not (Whiteley, 2007). In their absence, the organizations will find it very difficult to come up with a unified plan. In this article, mission and vision statement of Sears Holdings is analyzed.

Sears Holdings’ mission statement assert that the corporation is focused on expanding their businesses by means of offering excellent goods and services at a huge value when and where their clients require them, and by creating optimistic, permanent relations with their clients (Shop internationally at Sears, 2014 ).

On the other hand, the corporation’s vision is to be the favored and be the most reliant store for goods and services that improve home and family lives. Based on the above mission and vision statements, the organization aims are augmenting their clients’ trust, acting with honesty in all they do, treating all persons fairly, being answerable for their acts, and winning as a group.

Currently, there are over 4000 Sears’s stores in North America. Despite its growth, the company is currently fighting to gain profits. At the present, the company’s production is worsening on all levels amid a cutthroat environment. In the recent past, the company recorded murky Q1 incomes resulting in a huge net loss of $2.62 per share (Shop internationally at Sears, 2014 ) .

The precipitous slide was way below what the analysts had anticipated at a loss of $0.60 per share. In the same report, the company’s revenues had decreased by nine percent to $8.74 billion. The slide was below what financial forecasters had predicted at $8.74 billion. The company’s management team blamed the adverse weather for the losses. However, their claims fail to validate for the deterioration in the struggling Kmart sections.

The company’s financial records indicate that the corporation sales have been declining for the past six years. The only optimistic performance was that the company recorded a growth of 20% in its online sales (Shop internationally at Sears, 2014 ) . Nonetheless, an increase in online sales does not imply that the company is in a turnaround process. Without immediate interventions, the company is expected to perform poorly through to the year 2016.

To reduce on the losses and to stage a comeback, the corporation has put in place measure that will ensure that it gets lean, focus on men’s clothing, and concentrate more on their core services.

Notably, for the last few years the organization has been able to operate majorly owing to trades of its real estate section. The shutdown of a number of its Kmart stores has helped the corporation reduce its operation costs. However, the shutdown of a number of its store is not enough for the company to get lean. The company should invest hugely in the remaining stores.

Equally, strict inventory management has helped the company from increasing its losses. Despite this, it is apparent that Sears is short of the one vital thing that will enable it to turnaround. As such, the company should come up with an appropriate plan that will enable it to reverse the declining losses and return to their prestigious position in the market. Through this, the corporations can be able to implement actions that guide their businesses forward and keep away from allocating capital to actions that do not.

A good vision statement should indicate what the business is all about, where the business wants to be in the future, the clients the organizations wants to engage relate to, and connect with the mission and be different from it (Carpenter, Bauer, & Erdogan, 2010).

Equally, a good mission statement should portray the organization’s reasons for operations and plans to satisfy the stakeholder’s needs. Based on the above requirements, Sears mission and vision does not require any revision. As such, its vision has captured where Sears wants to be in the future, the clients it plans to engage.

Similarly, Sears’ vision is related to its vision because it seeks to achieve what the mission highlighted. Therefore, the company’s dismal performance cannot be attributed to their mission statement or vision statement. Instead, the company’s management team should be blamed for failing to abide by the organization’s mission and vision. This has resulted in poor performance, declining sales, terrible management choices, and lack of concise efforts to advance branding plans.

References

Carpenter, M., Bauer, T., & Erdogan, B. (2010). Principles of management 1.1 . Irvington, NY: Flat World Knowledge. Shop internationally at Sears . (2014, January 15). Web.

Whiteley, A. M. (2007). Core values and organizational change: theory and practice . Hackensack, New Jersey: World Scientific.

The Renaissance period, which spanned from the 14th to the 17th century, was a time of immense cultural, artistic, and intellectual growth in Europe. This period marked a significant shift from the medieval era, as it brought about a renewed interest in the classical texts and ideas of ancient Greece and Rome. The Renaissance was a time of great innovation and creativity, and it laid the groundwork for many of the developments that would shape the modern world.

One of the most significant aspects of the Renaissance was the revival of interest in classical learning. During the medieval period, much of the knowledge and wisdom of the ancient world had been lost or forgotten. However, during the Renaissance, scholars and thinkers began to rediscover and study the works of ancient philosophers, scientists, and writers. This renewed interest in classical learning had a profound impact on European thought, as it led to the development of humanism, a philosophical and intellectual movement that emphasized the importance of human potential and achievement.

In addition to the revival of classical learning, the Renaissance was also a time of great artistic and cultural achievement. The period saw the emergence of some of the most celebrated artists and thinkers in history, including Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo, and Raphael. These artists created some of the most iconic works of art in the Western canon, and their contributions continue to be celebrated and studied to this day. The Renaissance also saw the development of new artistic techniques and styles, such as perspective and chiaroscuro, which had a lasting impact on the art world.

The Renaissance was also a time of great innovation and discovery. The period saw significant advancements in fields such as science, mathematics, and navigation. For example, the development of the printing press by Johannes Gutenberg in the 15th century revolutionized the spread of knowledge and information, making books and other written materials more accessible to a wider audience. Similarly, the work of scientists and explorers during the Renaissance laid the groundwork for many of the discoveries and advancements that would shape the modern world.

The significance of the Renaissance period extends beyond its cultural and intellectual achievements. The period also had a lasting impact on the political and social structures of Europe. The Renaissance saw the rise of powerful city-states such as Florence and Venice, which became important centers of trade, commerce, and culture. These city-states were often ruled by wealthy and influential families, such as the Medici in Florence, who were patrons of the arts and played a significant role in supporting the work of artists and thinkers.

Furthermore, the Renaissance also had a profound impact on the religious and spiritual life of Europe. The period saw the emergence of new religious and philosophical movements, such as the Protestant Reformation, which challenged the authority of the Catholic Church and led to significant changes in the religious landscape of Europe. The Renaissance also saw the development of new ideas and beliefs about the nature of the universe and humanity's place within it, leading to significant changes in the way people thought about themselves and the world around them.

In conclusion, the Renaissance period was a time of immense significance and importance in the history of Western civilization. The period saw a renewed interest in classical learning, the emergence of great artistic and cultural achievements, and significant advancements in science and exploration. The impact of the Renaissance continues to be felt to this day, as many of the developments and innovations of the period laid the groundwork for the modern world. The Renaissance was a time of great change and innovation, and its significance cannot be overstated.

Promotion of Pop Culture in the Mass Media Essay (Critical Writing)

The picture of the contemporary world is far from the previous evaluation of the main values which are so important for people. The growth of scientific and technological progress made a great impact on the cultural milieu in the United States. People are involved in a perpetual process of enculturation since new devices became important in society. Different technological inventions grew in their influence on society day by day, year by year until the critical point was achieved at the beginning of the twenty-first century.

The thing is that the purity of culture and its main objectives are influenced by mass media and, what is more, a contemporary man in the United States or somewhere in developed countries does not imagine life without the informational background or support of articles, films, shows, games. The invention of the Internet brought many values to society and made life easier in gaining information, but along with profits, this source gave society drawbacks as well. The paper is strictly dedicated to the analysis of how pop culture is related to mass media and how this mutual connection is evaluated by society.

Though, the medium is a sort of information delivery since the emergence of this term and its materialization in social relations. With the flow of time and progress mass character of media was constantly increasing within the society and now its growth and influence on public opinion are greater than ever. In other words, it shifted all expectations. Brands became more significant for people than real and more vital things. New generations of people apprehend to such innovations as the Internet and computer games and those effects which these sources of information may cause sooner or later. Parents are not aware of how to resist such crucial expansion of new technologies and technical implementation for entertaining.

When talking about the influence of mass media on pop culture it is necessary to represent examples when people intentionally or unintentionally subduing to the “syndrome of the crowd” let them be involved in the money-making machine on the base of mass media presentation of this or that product or service or organization. Of course, such initiatives need great sums of money, but still, it is needful to figure out the most distinctive examples of mass media way toward enculturation with this or that product.

The example of McDonald’s seems to be the one of the most appropriate for analysis. This company with the largest restaurant chain worldwide has its image and good reputation in the field of fast food. The peculiarity of this company is that in every subsidiary of McDonald’s you can find the same items of products suggested in this or that part of the world. Time went by and now it is a symbol of American easiness in the issue of quick and substantial nutrition. Mass media did everything for the purpose of enculturation of this product as a national brand for the American people and as a hint for imitation of proper manners in service and way of eating within people all around the world.

Being one of the cheapest ways to have a bite McDonald’s has become familiar with its family trend. A figure of clown and a baby-room which can be seen inside any of the company’s branches are advertised across-the-board by means of television, city-lights and other means for advertising. No one rejects the correspondence of cliché connected with McDonald’s with an American lifestyle and a sort of cultural approach. The phenomenon of McDonald’s impacts comprises its wide direction toward various layers of society (Alfino, Caputo, and Wynyard, 1998).

Another example contemplates the fact when media, advertising, and the formation of normative cultural values are united in a reciprocal connection. Here the issue concerns The Coca-Cola Company, one of the most popular and largest producers of soft drinks in the world. Today many people do not simply drink this beverage because of being thirsty. It became a pointer of one’s following the vogue tendency of label and brand. Advertisements concerning Coca-Cola have many points of joy and good time accompanied with the drink. Moreover, people got accustomed to the fact that Christmas is not possible without Santa Claus from the advertisement and without a row of trucks carrying bottles with a beverage. This feature of psychological impact is outlined with a proper evaluation of Coca-Cola’s significance within the masses. Christmas is a great celebration for families in the United States and other Western countries. Such a wise trick of the Coca-Cola Company was chosen successfully and now this cultural norm is taken for granted in American society.

Media Portrayal of Latinos in “Latinos Beyond Reel” Film Report

The documentary evaluates the portrayal of Latinos in US media. Latinos face an ethnic barrier that result in them being grossly underrepresented in movies and other forms of media. For instance, in the movie Scarface , white actors were hired to play Latino characters. In films where Latino and Hispanic people are featured, they are portrayed with certain offensive stereotypes. For example, they are shown to be drug dealers or violent gang members. This negative misrepresentation in the media perpetuates Latino stereotypes in the real world.

The main point of the video is that Latinos are negatively portrayed in US media. Men are shown to be violent, hotheaded, and often engaging in illegal activities. On the other hand, women are over-sexualized and in some cases, portrayed as prostitutes. Examples include in films and shows such as The Perez Family, Dogma, and Sin City . The effect of this is an increase in hate crimes against Latino and Hispanic people in the US.

The documentary also argues that the US media needs to represent Latinos in a more dignified manner. There are numerous examples of accomplished Latinos who are absent from the limelight. For example, the culture boasts of astronauts, politicians, judges, and sportsmen who do not receive as much media coverage as they should, considering their accomplishments ( Latinos Beyond Reel: Challenging a Media Stereotype ). Additionally, Latino characters are needed for children from this culture to have heroes who look like them. Overall, increased progressive depiction will have a positive impact on the nation.

I have observed the stereotypical depictions of Latinos, but I had not noticed they were underrepresented in media. Upon taking a closer look, I now see that the film makes valid points. I think that in an attempt at humor, the media does irreparable damage towards the Latino community. I have a friend of Latino heritage, and I have witnessed people making such stereotypical jokes at her expense. She usually brushes them off, but I can tell they make her uncomfortable. I think that even though the film was made almost a decade ago, it remains relevant today.

Question: What positive or dignified representations of Latinos have you seen in the US media?

Latinos Beyond Reel: Challenging a Media Stereotype. Directed by Chyng Sun and Miguel Parker, The Media Education Foundation, 2013.
